SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.claim: ‘I will come’ conveys resolve while ‘perhaps I will come’ conveys hope; ordinary speech can move from certainty to qualification as circumstances intervene, so the paired expressions are not contradictory.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r1.anchor: يقول أحدنا سآتي اليوم لعلي أستطيع بمعنى (أقطع ثم أترجّى)

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.claim: The certainty of al-Naml fits its atmosphere of strength and empowerment; al-Qasas is shaped by fear from before Moses’ birth, fitting the hopeful wording.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r2.anchor: المقام كله في سورة النمل مبني على القطع والقوة والتمكين أما سورة القصص فهي مبنيّة على الخوف

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.claim: A flaming shihab gives more warmth and light, whereas a jadhwa need not contain flame; the less assured ember suits al-Qasas’ fearful setting.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p100/r3.anchor: الشهاب هو شعلة من النار والشهاب أنفع في الدفء والإستنارة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.claim: He gives jadhwa as an ember or firebrand; other explanations call it wood remaining after burning or a stick with fire but no flame.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r1.anchor: فهي الجمرة أو القبسة من النار وقيل: هي ما يبقى من الحطب بعد الالتهاب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.claim: The shihab is better than the ember for warmth and illumination because it bears a bright flame.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r2.anchor: الشهاب يدفىء أكثر من الجمرة لما فيه من اللهب الساطع، كما أنه ينفع في الاستنارة أيضاً.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.claim: Saying he will fetch a shihab kindled from the fire signals resolve and courage; the less certain jadhwa suits fear, while the shihab fits a scene without fear.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p96/r3.anchor: وهذا أدلّ على القوة وثبات الجنان، لأن معناه أنه سيذهب إلى النار ويقبس منها شعلة ساطعة.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.claim: The repeated coming in al-Naml signals Moses’ confidence and strength; he does not repeat the verb in al-Qasas, fitting its fearful atmosphere.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r1.anchor: فأكد الإتيان في سورة النمل لقوة يقينه وثقته بنفسه، والتوكيد يدل على القوة، في حين لم يكرر فعل الإتيان في القصص مناسبة لجو الخوف

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.claim: The verb for coming appears twelve times in al-Naml and six in al-Qasas, so repeating ātiikum suits al-Naml throughout.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r2.anchor: إن فعل (الإتيان) تكرر في النمل اثنتي عشرة مرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r5.claim: Jadhwa means an ember or a piece of fire.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r5.anchor: وأما (الجذوة) فهي الجمرة أو القبسة من النار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r6.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r6.speaker: قيل
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r6.claim: Another reported definition is wood left after burning, or a stick with fire but no flame.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r6.anchor: وقيل: هي ما يبقى من الحطب بعد الالتهاب، وفي معناه ما قيل: هي عود فيه نار بلا لهب

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.claim: The bright flame is better than an ember because its blazing flame gives more warmth and also provides light.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r7.anchor: والمجيء بالشهاب أحسن من المجيء بالجمرة، لأن الشهاب يدفئ أكثر من الجمرة لما فيه من اللهب الساطع

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r9.claim: In al-Qasas Moses only says he may bring an ember; he does not say he will take it from the fire.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p74/r9.anchor: أما في القصص فقد ذكر أنه ربما أتى بجمرة من النار، ولم يقل إنه سيقبسها منها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.claim: Al-Naml uses the future sīn for emphasis and certainty, while al-Qasas uses laʿallī to express hope.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r1.anchor: في سورة النمل جاء بالسين في (سآتيكم) والسين تفيد التوكيد، أما في القصص فجاء بـ (لعلي آتيكم) وهي للترجّي

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.claim: Speakers can commit and then hope circumstances allow it, or the reverse; the scene determines whether the wording conveys hope or certainty.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r2.anchor: يقول أحدنا سآتي اليوم لعلي أستطيع بمعنى (أقطع ثم أترجّى)

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.claim: Al-Naml’s scene is built on certainty, strength, and empowerment; al-Qasas’ scene is built on fear reaching back to before Moses’ birth.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r3.anchor: المقام كله في سورة النمل مبني على القطع والقوة والتمكين أما سورة القصص فهي مبنيّة على الخوف من قبل ولادة موسى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.claim: A bright, warming, illuminating flame fits al-Naml’s confident scene; a mere ember that may not contain fire fits al-Qasas’ fearful scene.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r4.anchor: الشهاب أنفع في الدفء والإستنارة، أما في القصص فقال تعالى (أو جذوة من النار) والجذوة ليس بالضرورة أن يكون فيها نار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.claim: Quranic speech accurately conveys events in a highly crafted style; each wording is correct and shaped for its context, like choosing tactful terms when speaking to an elder.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p550/r5.anchor: القرآن هو ترجمة للأحداث والأقوال لكن مصوغ صياغة فنّية عالية

DAMGHANI:v1p255/r12.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p255/r12.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p255/r12.claim: Sāra means to travel; the work groups several commands and descriptions of travel.
DAMGHANI:v1p255/r12.anchor: سار أي سافر قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.claim: Qaḍā can mean completing a term or period, and completing the revelation sent to someone.
DAMGHANI:v1p383/r10.anchor: الثامن : قضى أتم قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r4.claim: Moses completed both agreements and the work term; a report says he chose the longer term, ten years.
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r4.anchor: فلما أتم الأجل المشروط بينهما وفرغ منه روي أنه قضى أبعد الأجلين

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r5.claim: Shuayb grieved at Moses's departure in his old age; Moses said he had been long absent from his mother, aunt, Aaron, and sister in Pharaoh's kingdom.
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r5.anchor: يا موسى كيف تخرج عني وقد ضعفت وكبرت؟ فقال له : قد طالت غيبتي

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r6.claim: Shuayb prayed by the honor of Abraham, Ishmael, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph for his strength and sight to be restored; Moses said amen and God restored them.
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r6.anchor: يا رب بحرمة إبراهيم الخليل وإسماعيل الصفي وإسحاق الذبيح

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r7.claim: Moses traveled toward Egypt with Shuayb's permission; سير means to move through the land.
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r7.anchor: موسى بإذن شعيب نحو مصر والسير المضي في الأرض

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r8.claim: His أهل were his wife Safuriyya and their child, whom she bore before the journey, according to Kashf al-Asrar; Kashifi reads the باء as causative, “he took his family.”

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r9.speaker: ابن عطاء
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r9.claim: Esoterically, after Moses completed the term of love and nearness approached, he traveled with his family so they could share in the subtleties of divine beneficence.
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لما تم له أجل المحبة

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r10.speaker: كشف الأسرار
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r10.claim: It was a dark, cold night with rain and snow; Moses camped by a valley, his sheep scattered in the storm, and his pregnant wife went into labor. He tried to kindle a fire but could not.
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r10.anchor: وكان في البرية والليلة مظلمة باردة فضرب خيمته على الوادي

BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r11.claim: Moses saw a fire from the direction facing the mountain; جانب means the side toward something, and al-Tur is a particular mountain; النار can denote visible flame, bare heat, or Hellfire.
BURSEVI:v6p290#2/r11.anchor: أبصر من الجهة التي تلي الطور نارا يقال جانب الحائط للجهة

BURSEVI:v6p291/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p291/r1.claim: Some say Moses saw fire as a sign of lights: divine light appeared dressed as fire to match his need and familiar desire in winter; Gabriel likewise often appeared as Dihya because the Prophet loved him.
BURSEVI:v6p291/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : أبصر نارا دالة على الأنوار

BURSEVI:v6p291/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p291/r2.claim: The speaker of قال is Moses.

BURSEVI:v6p291/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p291/r3.claim: Amkuthu means to remain and wait, so Moses told his family to stay where they were.
BURSEVI:v6p291/r3.anchor: المكث ثبات مع انتظار أي قفوا مكانكم واثبتوا

BURSEVI:v6p291/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p291/r4.claim: He hoped to bring news from people by the fire about which way led to Egypt, since the travelers had lost their route.
BURSEVI:v6p291/r4.anchor: بيامي يعني از نزد كساني كه برسر آن آتش اند بيارم خبر طريق

BURSEVI:v6p291/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p291/r5.claim: Jadhwa is a thick piece of wood, whether or not it still has fire; al-Mufradat defines it as wood remaining after burning.
BURSEVI:v6p291/r5.anchor: عود غليظ سواء كانت في رأسه نار أو لا

BURSEVI:v6p291/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291/r6.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v6p291/r6.claim: The journey signifies outward detachment from family, property, and the world, and inward separation from attachment to both worlds; as attachment falls away, signs of unity appear, first as Moses's flame or Abraham's star, then as flashes, suns, and moons until the light of lordship appears.
BURSEVI:v6p291/r6.anchor: تشير الآية إلى التجريد في الظاهر وإلى التفريد في الباطن

BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r1.claim: Iṣṭilā means warming oneself at a fire; the noun ṣalāʾ has alternative vowelings and corresponding short or long forms.
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r1.anchor: الاصطلاء التدفؤ بالصلاء وهو النار بفتح الصاد وكسرها

BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r2.speaker: نجم الدين
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r2.claim: Human qualities are frozen by nature's cold and warm only through the spark of love or the fire of divine attraction.
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r2.anchor: يشير إلى أن أوصاف الإنسانية جامدة من برودة الطبيعة

BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r3.speaker: الكمال الخجندي
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r3.claim: His verse says a heart that has not burned in love is unworthy of the beloved's gaze.
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r3.anchor: دلي كه سوخته آتش محبت نيست

BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r4.claim: Moses left his family and went to the fire; when he arrived, the call came from the right bank relative to him, a place where water flows between mountains, hence called a valley.
BURSEVI:v6p291#2/r4.anchor: فترك موسى أهله في البرية وذهب

QASHANI:28:29-30/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:29-30/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:29-30/r1.claim: Completing Moses's term means perfection, the shorter term; traveling with family means bringing every faculty to the sacred realm through struggle and watchfulness.
QASHANI:28:29-30/r1.anchor: أي: بلغ حد الكمال الذي هو أقصر الأجلين

QASHANI:28:29-30/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:28:29-30/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:28:29-30/r2.claim: The mount is the secret, the fire is the Holy Spirit, and the blessed spot is the perfected heart or secret arising from its holy self.
QASHANI:28:29-30/r2.anchor: طور السر الذي هو كمال القلب في الارتقاء نار روح القدس

QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r1.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r1.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r1.claim: When God intends an event, He arranges its fitting causes; Moses first feared a trial, but the fire led him to prophethood through hidden decree.
QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r1.anchor: ولو لم تقع تلك الحالة لم يخرج موسى عندها بإيناس النار

QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r2.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r2.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r2.claim: God first showed fire and then light, but neither was the aim; the purpose was Moses hearing God say He is Lord of the worlds.
QUSHAYRI:v2p436/r2.anchor: ولا كان المقصود النار ولا النور . وإنما سماع نداء

SULAMI:v2p104#4/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r1.claim: When Moses's period of love ended and nearness and prophetic lights approached, he traveled with his family so they could share in God's subtle acts.
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r1.anchor: قال ابن عطاء : لما تم له اجل المحبة ودنا أيام القربة والزلفة وإظهار أنوار النبوة عليه

SULAMI:v2p104#4/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r2.speaker: جعفر
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r2.claim: Moses saw light in the form of fire; drawing near, sacred lights and intimacy enveloped him, and God addressed him, granted what he asked, and secured him from fear.
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r2.anchor: قال جعفر : أبصر نارا دلته على الأنوار لأنه رأى النور على هيئة النار

SULAMI:v2p104#4/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r3.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r3.claim: Moses described the fire as familiar rather than frightening; the place's purity and the divine conversation brought him into intimacy.
SULAMI:v2p104#4/r3.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن طاهر : آنس سره برؤية النار لما كان فيه من عظيم الشأن

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p332#4/r1.claim: جذوة means a piece of firewood; it is like جذمة, and exegesis describes it as a stick that has burned.

MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r1.claim: جذوة is a thick piece of wood with no flame; its plural is الجذا, and Ibn Muqbil's poem uses the term.
MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r1.anchor: «أو جذوة من النار» (29) أي قطعة غليظة من الحطب

MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r2.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r2.speaker: ابن مقبل
MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r2.claim: Ibn Muqbil's poem uses الجذا for large pieces of firewood.
MAJAZ:v2p102#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن مقبل: باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها ... جزل الجذا

NAHHAS:v3p236/r6.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p236/r6.speaker: عاصم
NAHHAS:v3p236/r6.claim: Asim reads جذوة with fatḥa on jīm.
NAHHAS:v3p236/r6.anchor: وقرأ عاصم 29 بفتح الجيم وروي عن الأعمش

NAHHAS:v3p236/r7.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p236/r7.speaker: الأعمش
NAHHAS:v3p236/r7.claim: A reading from al-Aʿmash gives جذوة with damma on jīm.
NAHHAS:v3p236/r7.anchor: وروي عن الأعمش ( أو جذوة ) بضم الجيم

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r1.speaker: النبي ﷺ، أبو ذر
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r1.claim: The Prophet told Abu Dharr to answer that Moses fulfilled the better and more completely of the two terms.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r1.anchor: عن أبي ذر - رضي الله عنه - قال لي رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - : يا أبا ذر ، ان سئلت اي الاجلين قضى موسى ؟ فقل : خيرهما واوفاهما .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ، ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r2.claim: When asked which term Moses completed, the Prophet answered that it was the more complete one.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، ان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سال جبريل : اي الاجلين قضى موسى ؟ اتمهما واكملهما .

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r3.speaker: النبي ﷺ، جبريل
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r3.claim: One report has Gabriel ask a higher angel and God answer that Moses completed the more virtuous and lasting term.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r3.anchor: عن يوسف بن سرج ، ان رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - سئل اي الاجلين قضى موسى فسال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - جبريل - عليه السلام - فقال : لا علم لي

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r4.speaker: النبي ﷺ، عتبة بن الندر
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r4.claim: Moses served for chastity and food; his father-in-law gave him newborn sheep, which multiplied and bore varied colors after Moses placed his staff at the trough.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2970/r4.anchor: عتبة بن الندر السلمي صاحب رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يحدث ان رسول الله

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r1.speaker: ابن لهيعة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r1.claim: Ibn Lahi'a defines five livestock types: al-fashush has freely flowing milk and a large yield; al-tanub has a long dragging udder; al-azuz yields little; al-tha'ul has only two teat-like nubs; al-kamsha has an udder too small for a hand to grasp.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r1.anchor: فسالت ابن لهيعة : ما الفشوش ؟ قال : التي تفش بلبانها ، وسعة الشخب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r2.claim: Mujahid says Moses completed the agreed term after ten years, then stayed another ten years.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد ، قوله : فلما قضى موسى الاجل عشر سنين ، ثم مكث بعد ذلك عشرا اخرى

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses traveled with his family, lost the way, and was traveling in winter.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r3.anchor: قال : قال عبد الله بن عباس : فلما قضى موسى الاجل سار باهله ، فضل الطريق وكان في الشتاء

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r4.claim: Qatada explains Moses perceived a fire on the side of the Mount.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r4.anchor: عن قتادة ، قوله : فلما قضى موسى الاجل وسار باهله انس من جانب الطور نارا اي احس من جانب الطور نارا

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r5.claim: Qatada also reports that the Prophet was traveling in cold winter weather.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r5.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : اني انست نارا اي احسست نارا - سار نبي الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - حين سار وهو شات

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says that if Moses found no news at the fire, he would bring a burning brand.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r6.anchor: قال : قال عبد الله بن عباس : لعلي اتيكم منها بخبر فان لم اجد خبرا اتيكم بشهاب قبس

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r7.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the travelers had lost their way and hoped to find someone by the fire who could guide them.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2971/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، قال : كانوا شاتين ، وكانوا قد ضلوا الطريق فلما راى النار ، قال : لعلي اتيكم منها بخبر

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r2.claim: Mujahid describes a jadhwa as the burning end of a branch.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r2.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح ، عن مجاهد جذوة من النار اصل الشجرة في طرفها النار

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses a jadhwa as a flame or burning brand.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2972/r3.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة ، عن ابن عباس ، قوله : جذوة من النار يقول : بشهاب

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r4.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r4.claim: Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd defines a jadhwa as a piece of firewood that still contains fire.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r4.anchor: الجذوة : عود من الحطب الذي فيه نار ذاك الجذوة

IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r5.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r5.claim: Al-Suddi explains the purpose of carrying fire as warming themselves against the cold.
IBNABIHATIM:v9p2973/r5.anchor: عن السدي لعلكم تصطلون قال : من البرد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.claim: The Madyan episode displays virtues that prepared Moses for revelation: generosity, helping the distressed, compassion, modesty, gratitude, chastity, and fidelity; Shuaib likewise shows hospitality, protection of the fearful, and gentleness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r1.anchor: هو ما تضمنته من فضائل الأعمال ومناقب أهل الكمال

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.claim: These character traits could lead Meccan polytheists to compare Moses with Muhammad's known virtue before his mission and recognize the signs of revelation; Muslims should also emulate prophetic character.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r2.anchor: ليعتبر المشركون بذلك إن كان لهم اعتبار في مقايسة تلك الأحوال بأجناسها من أحوال النبي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r6.claim: Exodus says Moses asked his father-in-law to go to Egypt to visit his family; the Quran's fire from the mountain adds what the account at 27:7 also relates.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v20p110/r6.anchor: أنه استأذن صهره في الذهاب إلى مصر لافتقاد أخته وآله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel, who said Moses fulfilled ten years.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r9.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل في ذلك جبريل فأخبره أنه قضى عشر سنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r10.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Mujahid that Moses served ten years plus another ten.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p285/r10.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن مجاهد أنه قضى عشرا وعشرا بعدها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r1.claim: The author calls the twenty-year report weak; Moses set out with his family for Egypt, his homeland and people, after sensing his prophetic selection.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r1.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف وفي قصص هذه الآية

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r2.speaker: النقاش
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r2.claim: Al-Naqqash says a Friday night brought lost fire, an unlit flint, a lost road, and severe cold; the light Moses saw was from God blended into a tree.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r2.anchor: قال النقاش كانت ليلة جمعة فقدوا النار وأصلد الزند وضلوا الطريق واشتد عليهم الخصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r3.speaker: وهب وقتادة وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r3.claim: They identify the tree respectively as oleander, hawthorn, or acacia; other reports name azarole or another species.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r3.anchor: قال وهب كانت عليقا وقال قتادة عوسجا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r4.claim: Ānasa means sensed, here by sight; the same word occurs for perceiving maturity in 4:6, and Hassan's line illustrates the usage.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r4.anchor: و «آنس» معناه أحس والإحساس هنا بالبصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r5.claim: Al-Ṭūr is a known mountain in Syria; ṭūr can mean any mountain, though some specify a mountain without vegetation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r5.anchor: وكان هذا الأمر كله في جانب الطور وهو جبل معروف بالشام،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r6.claim: Moses hoped to find directions or news of the route, or a burning coal from a large piece of wood, not a flame, to warm themselves.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r6.anchor: فقال لأهله أقيموا فقد رأيت نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر عن الطريق أين هو أو جذوة وهي القطعة من النار

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r7.speaker: ابن مقبل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r7.claim: Ibn Muqbil's line is cited for a large, dense piece of fuel that does not burn weakly or with a fierce flame.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r7.anchor: ومن ذلك قول الشاعر [ابن مقبل] : [البسيط] باتت حواطب ليلى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r8.claim: The author supposes the original sense of jadhwa is tree roots used as fuel in the desert, supported by al-Sulami's line about smoke from roots.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r8.anchor: وأحسب أن أصل «الجذوة» أصول الشجر وأهل البوادي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r9.speaker: حمزة والأعمش وعاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r9.claim: They give three dialect readings of jadhwa: kasra for most readers, ḍamma for Hamza and al-Aʿmash, and fatḥa for ʿAsim.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r9.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «جذوة» بكسر الجيم، وقرأ حمزة والأعمش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r10.claim: Al-ṣalā means the heat of fire; taṣṭalūn derives from it with tāʾ changed to ṭāʾ.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p286/r10.anchor: والصلى حر النار، وتصطلون تفتعلون منه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas transmits that when asked which term Moses completed, the Prophet said he fulfilled the fuller and better one.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r1.anchor: روى ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه سئل أي الأجلين قضى موسى قال أوفاهما وأطيبهما

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says Moses stayed with the family for ten further years after completing the term.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد مكث بعد قضاء الأجل عندهم عشرا أخر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r3.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r3.claim: Wahb ibn Munabbih says Moses stayed there for years after bringing his wife into the household.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r3.anchor: وقال وهب بن منبه أقام عندهم بعد أن أدخل عليه امرأته سنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafiʿ, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and al-Kisaʾi read jidhwa with kasra; ʿAsim uses fatḥa; Hamza, Khalaf, and al-Walid from Ibn ʿAmir use ḍamma. All are dialect forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r4.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي جذوة بكسر الجيم

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says a jidhwa is a piece of wood with fire; Abu ʿUbayda calls it a thick piece of wood without flame, like the stump of a tree.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r5.anchor: قال ابن عباس الجذوة قطعة حطب فيها نار وقال أبو عبيدة قطعة غليظة من الحطب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r6.speaker: ابن مقبل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r6.claim: Ibn Muqbil’s poem uses jazl al-jadhā for substantial, sound firewood, supporting Abu ʿUbayda’s lexical explanation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r6.anchor: باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا دعر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r7.claim: The wording through “or a brand” was already explained in the commentary on 20:10.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p217#2/r7.anchor: وقد سبق تفسير هذه الآية طه إلى قوله ﴿ أو جذوة ﴾

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r1.claim: Earlier discussion concluded Moses completed the fuller and better of the two terms; this verse's wording may also support that conclusion.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r1.anchor: قضى أتم الأجلين وأوفاهما وأبرهما وأكملهما وأنقاهما

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r2.speaker: مجاهد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r2.claim: Mujāhid says Moses served ten years and then another ten; Ibn Kathīr has not found this view elsewhere, though Ibn Jarīr and Ibn Abī Ḥātim cite him for it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r2.anchor: قضى عشر سنين، وبعدها عشرا أخر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r3.claim: Moses longed for his homeland and family, traveled secretly from Pharaoh with his wife and his father-in-law's sheep, and lost the road on a cold, rainy, dark night.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r3.anchor: كان موسى قد اشتاق إلى بلاده وأهله، فعزم على زيارتهم في خفية من فرعون

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r4.claim: He seeks news because he is lost or an ember to warm the family; the fire is on the mountain's western side to his right when facing the qiblah, in a green tree by the valley.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r5.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿūd describes the tree from which Moses was called as a fresh, green samurah tree; Ibn Kathīr calls the chain fair.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r5.anchor: عبد الله قال: رأيت الشجرة التي نودي منها موسى، عليه السلام، سمرة خضراء ترف. إسناده مقارب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r6.speaker: وهب بن منبه
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r6.claim: A report from Wahb calls the tree a ʿullayq, while some People of the Book say it was an ʿawsaj.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p234/r6.anchor: شجرة من العليق، وبعض أهل الكتاب يقول: من العوسج

JISHUMI:v8p5488/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5488/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5488/r6.claim: Īnās means seeing something that feels familiar or reassuring; a jadhwah is a thick piece of wood with fire, like the root of a tree.
JISHUMI:v8p5488/r6.anchor: والجذوة: الغليظة من الحطب فيها النار، وهي مثل الجذوة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r1.claim: Asked which term Moses completed, the Prophet answered that he fulfilled the farther and longer one.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r1.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : أي الأجلين قضى موسى ؟ فقال : ( أبعدهما وأبطأهما

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r2.claim: A second report says Moses fulfilled the more complete term and married the younger daughter; al-Zamakhshari notes this conflicts with the preceding report.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r2.anchor: قضى أوفاهما ، وتزوج صغراهما ) وهذا خلاف الرواية التي سبقت

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r3.claim: Jadhwah means a thick stick of wood, whether or not it has fire at its end.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r3.anchor: العود الغليظ ، كانت في رأسه نار أو لم تكن

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r4.claim: The word jadhwah is read in all three reported linguistic forms.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r4.anchor: باللغات الثلاث . وقرىء بهن جميعا : العود الغليظ

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r5.speaker: كثير
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r5.claim: Kuthayyir's verse uses jadhā for large pieces of firewood and supports the word's meaning.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r5.anchor:
قال كثير :
باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها … جزل الجذى غير خوار ولا دعر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r6.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r6.claim: An unattributed verse uses jadhwah for a burning brand and describes its heat and blaze.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p411#2/r6.anchor: وألقى على قبس من النار جذوة … شديدا عليه حرها والتهابها

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r1.claim: The first and second min mark the point of origin: the call came from the valley's bank, from beside the tree.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r1.anchor: من } الأولى والثانية لابتداء الغاية ، أي : أتاه النداء من شاطىء الوادي من قبل الشجرة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r2.claim: Min al-shajarah is an appositive of inclusion for the valley bank, since the tree grew on the bank; he cites 43:33 as a parallel construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r2.anchor: من الشجرة } بدل من قوله : من شاطىء الوادي ، بدل الاشتمال ؛ لأن الشجرة كانت نابتة على الشاطى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r3.claim: Al-buqah is read with either a dammah or a fathah.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r4.claim: Rahb has four reported vowel patterns and means fear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r4.anchor: و { الرهب } بفتحتين ، وضمتين ، وفتح وسكون ، وضم وسكون : وهو الخوف

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r5.claim: One explanation is that Moses recoiled from the transformed serpent and shielded himself with his hand; he was told to tuck the hand beneath his arm, avoiding a shameful appearance before enemies while displaying another miracle.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r5.anchor: لما قلب الله العصا حية : فزع واضطرب ، فاتقاها بيده كما يفعل الخائف من الشي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r6.claim: On this explanation, janah means hand because human hands are like a bird's wings; the right hand tucked under the left arm is a wing drawn inward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r6.anchor: والمراد بالجناح : اليد ؛ لأن يدي الإنسان بمنزلة جناحي الطائر

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r7.claim: A second explanation takes drawing in the wing as an order to steady and control oneself when the staff becomes a serpent, so Moses will not panic or fear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r7.anchor: والثاني : أن يراد بضم جناحه إليه : تجلده وضبطه نفسه . وتشدده عند انقلاب العصا حية حتى لا يضطرب ولا يرهب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r8.claim: The self-control interpretation is a bird metaphor: a frightened bird spreads and slackens its wings, while normally keeping them tucked and raised.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r8.anchor: استعارة من فعل الطائر ؛ لأنه إذا خاف نشر جناحيه وأرخاهما . وإلا فجناحاه مضمومتان إليه مشمران

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r9.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r9.claim: In an anecdote, he comforted an embarrassed scribe who had accidentally passed wind, telling him to take up his pen, draw in his wing, and calm down.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r9.anchor: خذ قلمك ، واضمم إليك جناحك ، وليفرخ روعك ، فإني ما سمعتها من أحد أكثر مما سمعتها من نفسي

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r10.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r10.claim: Min al-rahb means because of fear: fear at seeing the serpent is the cause for drawing in the wing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r10.anchor: ومعنى قوله : ( من الرهب ) من أجل الرهب ، أي : إذا أصابك الرهب عند رؤية الحية فاضمم إليك جناحك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r11.claim: Drawing in the wing and putting the hand into the garment can describe the same action; the different wording serves the distinct goals of showing a white hand and concealing fear.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r11.anchor: معنى : { واضمم إليك جناحك } ، وقوله : { اسلك يدك فى جيبك } على أحد التفسيرين : واحد . ولكن خولف بين العبارتين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r12.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r12.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r12.claim: The two commands about drawing the wing together are reconciled by taking the right hand as the wing drawn in and the left hand as the wing it is drawn toward; each hand can be called a wing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r12.anchor: المراد بالجناح المضموم . هو اليد اليمنى ، وبالمضموم إليه : اليد اليسرى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r13.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r13.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r13.claim: He rejects the claim that rahb means sleeve in Himyaritic, questioning its reliable attestation, contextual fit, and the claim that Moses wore a sleeveless wool garment.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r13.anchor: ومن بدع التفاسير : أن الرهب : الكم ، بلغة حمير

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r14.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r14.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r14.claim: Dhanak is read lightly as the dual of dhaka or with doubling as the dual of dhalika.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r14.anchor: فذانك } قرىء مخففا ومشددا ، فالمخفف مثنى ذاك . والمشدد مثنى ذلك

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r15.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r15.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r15.claim: The two proofs are clear and radiant; burhan is named for its brightness, like the term for a very fair woman.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r15.anchor: برهان } حجتان بينتان نيرتان . فإن قلت : لم سميت الحجة برهانا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r16.claim: The n in burhan is extra, as shown by abraha for bringing a proof; the term evokes whiteness and illumination.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r16.anchor: لبياضها وإنارتها من قولهم للمرأة البيضاء . برهرهة ، بتكرير العين واللام معا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r17.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r17.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r17.claim: Sultan is another name for proof, derived from salit, oil, because proof gives light.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p412/r17.anchor: ونظيره تسميتهم إياها سلطان من السليط وهو الزيت ، لإنارتها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r1.claim: Moses completed the term of service he had agreed to fulfill.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r2.claim: His family consisted of his wife.

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r3.claim: Ānasa means he saw, and seeing may also be expressed as knowing or perceiving.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r3.anchor: أي رأى , وقد يعبر عن الرؤية بالعلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r4.claim: Moses may have sought news whether his intended route was straight or diverted.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r4.anchor: بخبر الطريق الذي أراد قصده هل هو على صوبه أو منحرف عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r5.claim: Alternatively, he sought news whether the fire he saw promised comfort or danger.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r5.anchor: بخبر النار التي رأها هل هي لخير يأنس به أو لشر يحذره

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r6.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r6.claim: A jadhwa is a burning stump of wood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r6.anchor: الجذوة أصل الشجرة فيها نار , قاله قتادة

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r7.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r7.claim: A jadhwa is a stick with one burning part and one unburned part.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r7.anchor: أنها عود في بعضه نار وليس في بعضه نار , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r8.speaker: زيد بن أسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r8.claim: A jadhwa is a stick with fire but no flame.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r8.anchor: أنها عود فيه نار ليس له لهب , قاله زيد بن أسلم

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r9.claim: A jadhwa is a flaming meteor or firebrand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p249/r9.anchor: أنها شهاب من نار ذي لهب , قاله ابن عباس

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p250/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p250/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p250/r1.claim: A poetic line uses jadhwa for a burning brand held over an ember.
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p250/r1.anchor: وألقي على قبس من النار جذوة … شديد عليها حميها

MAWARDI-FULL:v4p250/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p250/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v4p250/r2.claim: Taṣṭalūn means that the family may warm themselves.

MUQATIL:28:29/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:29/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:29/r1.claim: After ten years, Moses traveled with his family on Friday night, saw a light by Mount Sinai, and sought directions or a burning branch to warm them because he had lost his way.
MUQATIL:28:29/r1.anchor: { فلما قضى موسى الأجل } السنين العشر، { وسار بأهله } ليلة الجمعة { آنس } يعني رأى

MUQATIL:28:29/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:28:29/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:28:29/r2.claim: Moses left his wife, child, and flock in the wilderness between Egypt and Midian; she remained there thirty years until a shepherd found her and took her to her father.
MUQATIL:28:29/r2.anchor: فترك موسى، عليه السلام، امرأته وولده في البرية بين مصر ومدين، ثم استقام

NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r1.claim: A Prophetic report says Moses completed the longer term and married the younger daughter, contrary to the narrative reported earlier.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r1.anchor: قال عليه السلام قضى اوفاهما وتزوج صغراهما وهذا بخلاف الرواية التي مرت

NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r2.claim: Moses traveled with his wife toward Egypt after finishing the term.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r2.anchor: بامرأته نحو مصر قال ابن عطاء لما أتم أجل المحنة ودنا أيام الزلفة

NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAṭāʾ reads the completed ordeal and journey as nearing intimacy with God and the light of prophethood, so Moses' family shares in subtle divine acts.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عطاء لما أتم أجل المحنة ودنا أيام الزلفة وظهرت أنوار النبوة سار باهله ليشتركوا معه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r4.claim: He saw fire at Mount Sinai and asked his family to wait while he sought directions because they had lost the road, or a burning brand to warm themselves.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p234#2/r4.anchor: ﴿ آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر ﴾ عن الطريق

QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.claim: Anistu means perceived or saw, as in Moses seeing a fire; al-Azhari explains the idiom as looking to see whether anyone is there, and al-Nabigha's wild bull poem illustrates watchful looking.
QURTUBI-FULL:4:6#5/r2.anchor:
أي أبصرتم ورأيتم ومنه قوله تعالى
آنس من جانب الطور نارا

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r1.claim: In answer to which term Moses completed, Ibn Abbas says he fulfilled the longer and more complete one; Saʿīd ibn Jubayr relays the answer to a Christian, who affirmed it.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r2.claim: Another report says the Prophet asked Gabriel about the term, and Gabriel answered that Moses fulfilled ten years.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r2.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل في ذلك جبريل

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r3.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī transmits Mujāhid's view that Moses completed ten years and another ten beyond them; Ibn ʿAṭiyya calls it weak.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r3.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن مجاهد أنه قضى عشرا وعشرا بعدها قال ابن عطية: وهذا ضعيف

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r4.claim: The wording that Moses traveled with his family supports a husband's ability to take his wife where he wishes by his guardianship, unless he has made a binding agreement; marriage covenants especially deserve fulfillment.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r4.anchor: إلا أن يلتزم لها أمرا فالمؤمنون عند شروطهم

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r5.claim: The majority read jadhwa with kasra on the jīm; Ḥamza and Yaḥyā use ḍamma, and ʿĀṣim, al-Sulamī, and Zirr ibn Ḥubaysh use fatḥa.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r5.anchor: والجذوة بكسر الجيم قراءة العامة، وضمها حمزة ويحيى

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r6.speaker: مجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r6.claim: Mujāhid glosses the jadhwa as a piece of ember and says this is common Arabic usage.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r6.anchor: قال مجاهد في قوله تعالى: { أو جذوة من النار } أي قطعة من الجمر

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r7.speaker: الجوهري
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r7.claim: Al-Jawharī says the differently vocalized forms all mean a burning ember, with several plural forms.

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r8.speaker: أبو عبيدة
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r8.claim: Abū ʿUbayda says jadhwa is like jadhma: a thick piece of wood, whether or not fire remains at its end.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r8.anchor: والجذوة مثل الجذمة وهي القطعة الغليظة من الخشب

QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r9.speaker: ابن مقبل
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r9.claim: Ibn Muqbil's verse uses al-jidhā for large pieces of fuel that do not quickly go out.
QURTUBI-FULL:28:29/r9.anchor: جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا دعر

SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r1.claim: Hamza reads جذوة with ḍamma, Asim with fatḥa, and the others with kasra; these are dialect variants for a stick with fire at its end.
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r1.anchor: قرأ حمزة بضم الجيم. وعاصم بالفتح. والباقون بالكسر. وهي لغات في العود الذي في رأسه نار

SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r2.speaker: السلمي
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r2.claim: He cites poetry about burning sticks and smoke as evidence for the word جذى.
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r2.anchor:
قال السلمي:
3601 حمى حب هذي النار حب خليلتي
وحب الغواني فهو دون الحباحب

SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r3.speaker: ابن مقبل
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r3.claim: His line describes chosen logs that do not crackle or flare, supporting a restricted sense of جذى.
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r3.anchor:
قال ابن مقبل:
3602 باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها
جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا دعر

SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r4.claim: Some restrict جذوة to a stick burning without flame, while a poem attests that it can blaze; another says it may mean any thick log, but this verse means a burning one.
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r4.anchor: وقيده بعضهم فقال: في رأسه نار من غير لهب. قال ابن مقبل:

SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r5.claim: من النار modifies جذوة rather than attaching to آتيكم, because this fire is not the previously mentioned fire and Arabic repeats a noun with a pronoun or definite article.
SAMIN-DURR:28:29/r5.anchor: من النار } صفة ل جذوة، ولا يجوز تعلقها ب " آتيكم " كما تعلق به " منها "؛ لأن هذه النار ليست النار المذكورة

STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r8.claim: Moses encounters the fire, hears God, witnesses his first miracles, and asks that Aaron join him against Pharaoh.
STUDYQURAN:28:intro/r8.anchor: Then Moses encounters the fire from which he hears God speak to him; he has his first experience of the miracles

STUDYQURAN:28:29/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r1.speaker: Q, R
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r1.claim: Some commentators say Moses completed the full ten-year term and then stayed for another ten years.
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r1.anchor: Some say that Moses completed the term of the entire ten years and then stayed ten more (Q, R).

STUDYQURAN:28:29/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r2.claim: The account of Moses seeing the fire also appears at 20:9, 26:10, and 27:7.
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r2.anchor: The incident of Moses seeing the fire is also mentioned in 20:9; 26:10; 27:7.

STUDYQURAN:28:29/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r3.speaker: R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r3.claim: A firebrand is a burning log or branch used to start another fire.
STUDYQURAN:28:29/r3.anchor: A firebrand refers to a burning log or branch with which one might start another fire (R, Ṭ).

TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r1.claim: Moses completed the agreed term with his companion, the father-in-law who gave him his daughter in marriage; the term was the two had agreed upon.
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r1.anchor: وذكر أن الذي وفاه من الأجلين أتمهما وأكملهما، وذلك العشر الحجج

TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses completed the better and fullest of the two terms; reports also phrase this as the last term, understood as ten years.
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، قال: سألت ابن عباس: " أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟ قال: خيرهما وأوفاهما

TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Said ibn Jubayr that Moses fulfilled the longer and better term because a prophet does not break a promise; the Jewish questioner accepts the answer.
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: «قضى أكثرهما وأطيبهما، إن النبي إذا وعد لم يخلف»

TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas tells Said that eight years were binding, a prophet would not short the term, and God would fulfill the promise, so Moses served ten years.
TAB-FULL:v18p234#2/r4.anchor: فلقيت ابن عباس، فذكرت له الذي سألني عنه النصراني، فقال: «أما كنت تعلم أن ثمانيا واجب عليه

TAB-FULL:v18p237/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses pastured for his companion the greater and better portion of the term.
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، " {فلما قضى موسى الأجل} [القصص: 29] قال: حدث ابن عباس، قال: «رعى عليه نبي الله أكثرها وأطيبها»

TAB-FULL:v18p237/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r2.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r2.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi reports that the Prophet said Moses completed the more complete and most fully honored term.
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r2.anchor: عن أبي معشر، عن محمد بن كعب القرظي، قال: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟

TAB-FULL:v18p237/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas reports the Prophet saying Moses completed both the most complete and fullest term.
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r3.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: " سألت جبرائيل أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟

TAB-FULL:v18p237/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r4.claim: Mujahid reports the Prophet asked Gabriel, who consulted Israfil and God; the answer was that Moses fulfilled the most righteous and complete term.
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r4.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال مجاهد: إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل جبرائيل

TAB-FULL:v18p237/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r5.claim: Mujahid says Moses served ten years, then remained another ten years after completing the term.
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r5.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: " {فلما قضى موسى الأجل} [القصص: 29] قال: عشر سنين، ثم مكث بعد ذلك عشرا أخرى

TAB-FULL:v18p237/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r6.speaker: أنس
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r6.claim: Anas recounts Moses' companion promising him lambs born unlike their mothers' color; Moses raised a reflection by the water, the flock bolted, and nearly all lambs were born piebald.
TAB-FULL:v18p237/r6.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: ثنا أنس، قال: " لما دعا نبي الله موسى صاحبه إلى الأجل الذي كان بينهما

TAB-FULL:v18p238/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p238/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p238/r1.claim: After completing the term, Moses set out with his family toward his home in Egypt; ānasa means to see or sense, illustrated by al-Aʿshāʿj's line about seeing a bird near the mountain.
TAB-FULL:v18p238/r1.anchor: يعني بقوله: آنس: أبصر وأحس، كما قال العجاج

TAB-FULL:v18p238/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p238/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p238/r2.claim: Qatada glosses Moses' perception as sensing a fire.
TAB-FULL:v18p238/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، " {آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا إني آنست نارا} [القصص: 29] : أي أحسست نارا

TAB-FULL:v18p239/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r1.claim: Moses tells his family to wait; he hopes to return with news or a thick piece of wood carrying fire, like a stump, so they can warm themselves.

TAB-FULL:v18p239/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r2.claim: Ibn Muqbil's verse uses jadhā for thick fuel-wood and witnesses the meaning of jadhwah.
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r2.anchor: جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا دعر

TAB-FULL:v18p239/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r3.claim: Three Arab pronunciations are reported for jadhwah; al-Tabari prefers the best-known kasra reading of Hijaz, Basra, and some Kufans, without rejecting the less common fatḥa reading.
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r3.anchor: وبها قرأت قراء الحجاز والبصرة وبعض أهل الكوفة، وهي أشهر اللغات الثلاث

TAB-FULL:v18p239/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses jadhwah as a meteor or glowing ember.
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله " {أو جذوة من النار} [القصص: 29] يقول شهاب

TAB-FULL:v18p239/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r5.claim: Qatada explains jadhwah as the base of a tree with fire, and also as a flame or fire at a branch tip.
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، " {أو جذوة} [القصص: 29] والجذوة: أصل شجرة فيها نار

TAB-FULL:v18p239/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r6.claim: Mujahid says jadhwah is the base of a tree.
TAB-FULL:v18p239/r6.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله " {أو جذوة من النار} [القصص: 29] قال: أصل شجرة

TAB-FULL:v18p240/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p240/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p240/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd defines jadhwah as a piece of firewood with fire in it.
TAB-FULL:v18p240/r1.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {أو جذوة من النار} [القصص: 29] قال: الجذوة: العود من الحطب الذي فيه النار

ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r2.speaker: يروى
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r2.claim: A report says Moses completed the longer of the two terms, ten years.
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r2.anchor: يروى أنه قغسى أتئم الأجلين، وهو عشر سنين.

ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r3.claim: آنس means perceived or saw; Moses says he hopes to learn why the fire was lit.
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r3.anchor:
(آنس من جانب الطور نارا).
آنس علم وأبصر، يقال: قد آنست ذلك الشخص أي أبصرته.

ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r4.claim: جذوة is a thick piece of firewood; its vowel is read with ḍamma or fatḥa, among three dialect forms.
ZAJJAJ:v4p142/r4.anchor:
الجذوة القطعهة الغليظة من الحطب.
ويقرأ: أو جذوة بالضم، ويقال جذوة بالفتح.
فيها ثلاث لغات (2).

TABATABAI:28:29-30/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r1.claim: Moses completed the service term he owed Shuʿayb; a report says he completed the longer of the two terms.
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r1.anchor: المراد بقضائه الأجل إتمامه مدة خدمته لشعيب عليه السلام والمروي أنه قضى أطول الأجلين

TABATABAI:28:29-30/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r2.claim: Īnās means seeing, jadhwa is a piece of fire, and iṣṭilāʾ means warming oneself.
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r2.anchor: والإيناس الإبصار والرؤية، والجذوة من النار القطعة منها، والاصطلاء الاستدفاء

TABATABAI:28:29-30/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r3.claim: The scene is at night on a very cold night; the family had lost their way, and Moses saw a fire from the mountain side.
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r3.anchor: والسياق يشهد أن الأمر كان بالليل وكانت ليلة شديدة البرد وقد ضلوا الطريق فرأى من جانب الطور

TABATABAI:28:29-30/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r4.claim: The parallel in Ṭā Hā is stronger evidence that they had lost the road: Moses hopes to bring news, a firebrand, or guidance from the fire.
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r4.anchor: وقد وقع في القصة من سورة طه موضع قوله { لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر } الخ قوله لعلي آتيكم منها بقبس أو أجد على النار هدى طه 10

TABATABAI:28:29-30/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r5.claim: The plural command to remain shows that Moses had several companions with him, not merely one person.
TABATABAI:28:29-30/r5.anchor: وكذا في قوله خطابا لأهله { امكثوا } الخ، شهادة على أنه كان معها من يصح معه خطاب الجمع

TABATABAI:28:29-42/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r1.claim: The Qur'an prescribes one religion for its communities, listing Moses alongside Noah, Abraham, and Jesus among those to whom God revealed it.
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r1.anchor: شرع لكم من الدين ما وصى به نوحا والذي أوحينا إليك وما وصينا به إبراهيم وموسى وعيسى

TABATABAI:28:29-42/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r2.claim: Moses and Hārūn are included in the solemn covenant God took from the prophets and are both among those to whom the religion was prescribed.
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r2.anchor: وإذ أخذنا من النبيين ميثاقهم ومنك ومن نوح وإبراهيم وموسى وعيسى ابن مريم وأخذنا منهم ميثاقا غليظا

TABATABAI:28:29-42/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r3.claim: God says He bestowed favor on Moses and Hārūn and pronounces peace upon them.

TABATABAI:28:29-42/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r4.claim: Moses is described as sincere, a messenger and prophet, brought near in private speech, honored before God, and spoken to directly.
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r4.anchor: واذكر في الكتاب موسى إنه كان مخلصا وكان رسولا نبيا وناديناه من جانب الطور الأيمن وقربناه نجيا

TABATABAI:28:29-42/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r5.claim: The Qur'an also calls Moses and the other named prophets beneficent, righteous, favored, chosen, guided, and recipients of divine blessing.
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r5.anchor: فأخبر أنهم كانوا محسنين صالحين وأنه فضلهم على العالمين واجتباهم وهداهم الى صراط مستقيم

TABATABAI:28:29-42/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r6.claim: Taken together, these descriptions establish Moses' sincerity, nearness, standing, excellence, righteousness, distinction, election, guidance, and blessing; the book given to him is the Torah.
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r6.anchor: فاجتمع بذلك له عليه السلام معنى الإخلاص والتقريب والوجاهة والإحسان والصلاح والتفضيل والاجتباء والهداية والإنعام

TABATABAI:28:29-42/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r7.claim: The Torah is called a criterion, illumination, and reminder for the God-fearing, guidance and light, and the tablets contain admonition and detail.
TABATABAI:28:29-42/r7.anchor: وذكر الكتاب النازل عليه وهو التوراة فوصفها بأنها إمام ورحمة

TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r1.claim: The Torah was altered and became a subject of disagreement; histories recount Nebuchadnezzar's 588 BCE destruction of Jerusalem's temple, burning of the Torah, and exile, followed by Cyrus's 538 BCE return permission and Ezra's rewriting it.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r1.anchor: قصة بختنصر وفتحه فلسطين ثانيا وهدمه الهيكل وإحراقه التوراة وحشره اليهود إلى بابل سنة خمسمائة وثمان وثمانين قبل المسيح

TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r2.claim: Moses is the Qur'an's most frequently mentioned prophet, named 166 times and alluded to across 34 surahs; the Qur'an lists many of his extraordinary signs.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r2.anchor: فقد ذكر اسمه - على ما عدوه - ماءة وستة وستين موضعا من كلامه تعالى، وأشير إلى قصته إجمالا أو تفصيلا في أربع وثلاثين سورة

TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an recounts selected episodes from prophetic histories rather than every detail, choosing what serves guidance and admonition.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r3.anchor: من دون استيفائها في كل ما دق وجل بل بالاقتصار على فصول منها يهم ذكرها لغرض الهداية والإرشاد

TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r4.claim: Moses was born in Egypt to an Israelite family during Pharaoh's male infanticide; his mother placed him in a chest in the river, Pharaoh took him and returned him to her to nurse, and he grew up in Pharaoh's house.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r4.anchor: تولد بمصر في بيت إسرائيلي حينما كانوا يذبحون المواليد الذكور من بني إسرائيل بأمر فرعون وجعلت أمه إياه في تابوت

TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r5.claim: As an adult Moses killed an Egyptian, fled Egypt to avoid Pharaoh's punishment, stayed in Midian with the prophet Shuʿayb, and married one of his daughters.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#2/r5.anchor: ثم بلغ أشده وقتل القبطي وهرب من مصر إلى مدين خوفا من فرعون وملئه أن يقتلوه قصاصا

TABATABAI:28:29-42#3/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#3/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#3/r1.claim: On a wintry night after completing his term, Moses set out with his family, lost the road, and approached the fire seeking a firebrand or guidance; God called him from the right bank and commissioned him with signs to free Israel.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#3/r1.anchor: ثم لما قضى موسى الأجل وسار باهله آنس من جانب الطور نارا وقد ضلوا الطريق في ليلة شاتية

TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r1.claim: Another Qur'anic episode recounts Moses travelling with his attendant to the meeting of the two seas, meeting the righteous servant, accompanying him, and eventually parting from him.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r1.anchor: ومن قصص موسى عليه السلام ما ذكره الله في سورة الكهف من مضيه مع فتاه إلى مجمع البحرين للقاء العبد الصالح وصحبته حتى فارقه

TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r2.claim: God associates Hārūn with Moses in the gifts, Book, guidance, greeting of peace, excellence, and status among faithful servants, and calls Hārūn a messenger and prophet.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r2.anchor: أشركه الله تعالى مع موسى عليهما السلام في سورة الصافات في المن وإيتاء الكتاب، والهداية إلى الصراط المستقيم وفي التسليم

TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r3.claim: Moses prayed for Hārūn to strengthen him, share his task, and help them remember and glorify God; Hārūn remained beside Moses and helped with his aims.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r3.anchor: واجعل لي وزيرا من أهلي هارون أخي أشدد به أزري وأشركه في أمري كي نسبحك كثيرا ونذكرك كثيرا

TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r4.claim: The Qur'an's distinctive episode about Hārūn is his stewardship during Moses' absence; when Moses returned angry over the calf, Hārūn said the people had overpowered him and nearly killed him.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#4/r4.anchor: ولم يرد في القرآن الكريم مما يختص به من القصص إلا خلافته حين غاب عن القوم للميقات

TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r1.claim: The Torah says the people, worried because Moses delayed on the mountain, asked Hārūn to make gods to lead them.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r1.anchor: وذلك أنه لما رأى الشعب أن موسى أبطأ في النزول من الجبل اجتمع الشعب على هارون وقالوا له قم اصنع لنا آلهة

TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r2.claim: The Torah recounts that Hārūn told the people to remove their families' earrings and bring them to him.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r2.anchor: فقال لهم هارون انزعوا أقراط الشعب التي في آذان نسائكم وبنيكم وبناتكم وأتوني بها

TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r3.claim: It says the people handed over their gold, which Hārūn shaped and engraved into a cast calf.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r3.anchor: فنزع كل الشعب أقراط الذهب التي في آذانهم وأتوا بها إلى هارون فأخذ ذلك من أيديهم وصوره بالإزميل

TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r4.claim: The Qur'anic passages indirectly criticize the Torah's account in these episodes, a point clear to a reflective reader.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r4.anchor: وفي الآيات القرآنية تعريضات للتوراة في هذه المواضع من قصصه عليه السلام غير خفية على المتدبر فيها

TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r5.claim: The Torah says Hārūn made Israel's golden calf at the people's request by collecting their gold earrings and casting a calf; the Qur'an indirectly criticizes this account.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r5.anchor: ومنها أنها تذكر أن الذي صنع لهم العجل فعبدوه هو هارون النبي أخو موسى عليهما السلام

TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r6.claim: Other differences include both men in the second fight over Moses' killing being Israelites, Hārūn casting the staff, omission of the seventy men and their revival, and tablets of stone; the Qur'an also alludes critically to these accounts.
TABATABAI:28:29-42#5/r6.anchor: وهناك اختلافات جزئية كثيرة كما وقع في التوراة في قصة قتل القبطي أن المتضاربين ثانيا كانا جميعا إسرائيليين

TABRISI:28:28-29/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:28:28-29/r6.claim: Moses fulfilled the longer term; the Prophet is reported to have answered that he fulfilled the term that was fuller and longer.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r6.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: أي الأجلين قضى موسى

TABRISI:28:28-29/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r7.speaker: أبو ذر
TABRISI:28:28-29/r7.claim: The Prophet reportedly advised saying Moses fulfilled the better and more generous term, and married the younger sister who had asked their father to hire him.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r7.anchor: إذا سئلت أي الأجلين قضى موسى فقل خيرهما وأبرهما

TABRISI:28:28-29/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:28-29/r8.claim: The narrative omits that Moses finished his term, took his wife, and then headed toward Syria.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r8.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف وإيجاز وهو فلما قضى موسى الأجل وتسلم زوجته ثم توجه نحو الشام

TABRISI:28:28-29/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:28-29/r9.claim: One story says Moses received the staff from his father-in-law to protect the flock; another says Adam brought it from Paradise, Gabriel took it after Adam died, and later handed it to Moses, according to ʿIkrima.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r9.anchor: أمر الشيخ أن يعطي موسى عصا يدفع السباع عن غنمه بها

TABRISI:28:28-29/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r10.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:28:28-29/r10.claim: ʿIkrima says the staff came out of Paradise with Adam; Gabriel took it after Adam died and gave it to Moses at night.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r10.anchor: خرج آدم بالعصا من الجنة فأخذها جبرائيل بعد موت آدم ع

TABRISI:28:28-29/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:28-29/r11.claim: Another account says prophets inherited the staff until Shuʿayb gave it to Moses.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r11.anchor: لم يزل الأنبياء يتوارثونها حتى وصلت إلى شعيب فأعطاها موسى

TABRISI:28:28-29/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r12.speaker: عبد الله بن سنان
TABRISI:28:28-29/r12.claim: Ibn Sinan reports from Abu ʿAbdillah that Moses' staff was a myrtle branch from Paradise, brought by Gabriel as Moses headed for Midian.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r12.anchor: كانت عصا موسى قضيب آس من الجنة أتاه به جبرائيل عليه السلام لما توجه تلقاء مدين

TABRISI:28:28-29/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:28-29/r13.speaker: السدي
TABRISI:28:28-29/r13.claim: Al-Suddi says an angel disguised as a man had deposited the staff with Shuʿayb; his daughter could only hold that staff despite trying to bring another, so her father gave it to Moses.
TABRISI:28:28-29/r13.anchor: كانت تلك العصا استودعها شعيبا ملك في صورة رجل فأمر ابنته أن تأتيه بعصا

TABRISI:28:29-30/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:29-30/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:28:29-30/r1.claim: Moses stayed with his father-in-law for another ten years after the agreed term, twenty years total, then got leave to return to Egypt and visit his parents and brother.
TABRISI:28:29-30/r1.anchor: مكث بعد انقضاء الأجل عند صهره عشرا أخرى فأقام عنده عشرين سنة

TABRISI:28:29-30/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:29-30/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:29-30/r2.claim: Another account says Moses left after ten years with his wife and flock, avoiding the main route for fear of Syrian rulers; in a cold, dark wilderness his wife labored, the sheep scattered, and rain left him lost.
TABRISI:28:29-30/r2.anchor: لما قضى العشر سار بأهله أي بامرأته وبأولاد الغنم التي كانت له

TABRISI:28:29-30/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:29-30/r3.speaker: أبو بصير
TABRISI:28:29-30/r3.claim: Abu Baṣīr reports from Abu Jaʿfar that Moses, traveling with his family toward Jerusalem after the term, lost his way at night and saw a fire.
TABRISI:28:29-30/r3.anchor: لما قضى موسى الأجل وسار بأهله نحو بيت المقدس أخطأ الطريق ليلا فرأى نارا

TABRISI:28:29-30/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:29-30/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:29-30/r4.claim: Moses hoped to learn the route he intended and whether he was on course; alternatively, he sought to learn whether the fire signaled welcome or danger.
TABRISI:28:29-30/r4.anchor: بخبر من الطريق الذي أريد قصده وهل أنا على صوبه أو منحرف عنه

TABRISI:28:29-30/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:28:29-30/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:28:29-30/r5.claim: Jadhwa means a piece of fire, or the burning end of a tree; taṣṭalūn means to warm yourselves.

THALABI:v7p247/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p247/r1.claim: Moses completed the appointed term before setting out with his family.
THALABI:v7p247/r1.anchor: فلما قضى موسى الأجل أي أتمه وفرغ منه

THALABI:v7p247/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v7p247/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet said Moses fulfilled the longer and better of the two terms.
THALABI:v7p247/r2.anchor: سئل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟ قال: «أبعدهما وأطيبهما»

THALABI:v7p247/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v7p247/r3.claim: Utba ibn al-Tayyib reports the Prophet answered that Moses fulfilled the more righteous and fully honored term.
THALABI:v7p247/r3.anchor: وكان من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يسكن الشام، ومات

THALABI:v7p247#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v7p247#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Moses fulfilled the longer, better term, since a prophet does not break a promise; the Jewish questioner accepted the answer.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r1.anchor: فقال: قضى أكثرهما وأطيبهما، إن النبي إذا وعد لم يخلف

THALABI:v7p247#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r2.speaker: وهب
THALABI:v7p247#2/r2.claim: Wahb says Moses married the elder of the two daughters.

THALABI:v7p247#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
THALABI:v7p247#2/r3.claim: A further report says Moses married the younger daughter and fulfilled the full term; the author says this report, if sound, must be followed.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r3.anchor: وقد روي أن النبي (عليه السلام) قال: «تزوج صغراهما وقضى أوفاهما» فإن صح هذا الخبر فلا معدل عنه

THALABI:v7p247#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p247#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says Moses stayed another ten years after the first term, making twenty, then obtained leave to return to Egypt and visit his mother and brother.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: لما قضى موسى الأجل ومكث بعد ذلك عند صهره عشرا أخرى، فأقام عنده عشرين سنة

THALABI:v7p247#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p247#2/r5.claim: Moses traveled in winter by an indirect route to avoid Syrian kings; his pregnant wife might give birth at any hour, and darkness and severe cold impeded his journey.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r5.anchor: وكانت أيام الشتاء وأخذ على غير الطريق مخافة ملوك الشام، وامرأته في شهرها

THALABI:v7p247#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p247#2/r6.claim: Moses's flint failed to kindle a fire, so he saw a fire at the western right side of Mount Sinai on a dark, cold night.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r6.anchor: فقدح زندا فلم تور [المقدحة شيئا] ، ف آنس من جانب الطور نارا قال لأهله امكثوا

THALABI:v7p247#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r7.speaker: عاصم
THALABI:v7p247#2/r7.claim: The word jadhwa has three readings: fatḥ of jīm by Asim, ḍamm by Hamza, and kasr by the other readers.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r7.anchor: وفيها ثلاث لغات: فتح الجيم وهي قراءة عاصم،

THALABI:v7p247#2/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r8.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
THALABI:v7p247#2/r8.claim: Qatada and Muqatil define a jadhwa as a stick partly burned, with plural judhiyy.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r8.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل: الجذوة: العود الذي قد احترق بعضه، وجمعها جذي

THALABI:v7p247#2/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p247#2/r9.claim: The cited line by Ibn Muqbil uses judhā to mean large pieces of firewood.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن مقبل: باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها … جزل الجذي غير خوار ولا دعر

THALABI:v7p247#2/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p247#2/r10.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p247#2/r10.claim: Taṣṭalūn means to warm yourselves and shelter from the cold.
THALABI:v7p247#2/r10.anchor: لعلكم تصطلون أي تستدفئون وتستحمون بها من البرد

ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r1.claim: For the explanation of Moses’ desert wandering and of the fire allegory, Asad refers readers to his notes on 20:10 and 27:7-8.
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r1.anchor: For an explanation of Moses' wanderings in the desert, see note 7 on 20:10

ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r2.claim: Asad renders al-tur as Mount Sinai throughout because he understands the Qur’anic term to refer invariably to that mountain.
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n23/r2.anchor: the noun at-tur ("the mountain") is being rendered as "Mount Sinai"

ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n24/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n24/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n24/r1.claim: The omitted phrase means that Moses sought news about which route the family should take.
ASAD-NOTES:28:29#n24/r1.anchor: as to which way we are to pursue

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r1.speaker: أبو عمران الجوني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r1.claim: Abū ʿImrān al-Jawnī reports that Gabriel instructed the Prophet to say Moses fulfilled the longer and better term, and married the younger daughter.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r1.anchor: إن سألوك أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟ فقل: "أكثرهما وأفضلهما". وأي الجاريتين تزوج؟ فقال: "الصغرى منهما

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r2.speaker: القرظي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r2.claim: Al-Quraẓī reports that the Prophet said Moses completed the more fulfilling and complete of the two terms.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r2.anchor: وقال القرظي: سئل رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم-: أي الأجلين قضى موسى؟ قال: "أوفاهما وأتمهما"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r3.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r3.claim: A Jewish man asked Saʿīd ibn Jubayr which term Moses completed; Saʿīd referred the question to Ibn ʿAbbās, who answered ten years, the longer and better term, since a prophet does not break a promise; the Jew affirmed this.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r3.anchor: قضى أكثرهما وأطيبهما: عشرا؛ إن النبي إذا وعد لم يخلف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r4.speaker: مجاهد ومقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r4.claim: Mujāhid and Muqātil say Moses completed ten years, then requested and received his father-in-law’s permission to return to Egypt to visit his mother and brother; related material appears in Ṭā Hā and al-Naml.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p380/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد ومقاتل: {فلما قضى موسى الأجل} عشر سنين (¬2) {وسار بأهله}

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r1.speaker: author
