WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r1.claim: Jadhwa has three readings, with fatḥa, ḍamma, or kasra on the first consonant; all are dialect variants.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r1.anchor: فيها ثلاث قراءات: فتح الجيم، وضمها، وكسرها. وهي كلها لغات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda defines a jadhwa as a thick piece of wood without a flame and cites Ibn Muqbil’s line as evidence for the word.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r2.anchor: أبو عبيدة: الجذوة، مثل: الجذمة؛ وهي القطعة الغليظة من الخشب، ليس فيها لهب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r3.speaker: ابن مقبل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r3.claim: Ibn Muqbil’s verse is cited as poetic evidence for the word jadhā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r3.anchor:
ابن مقبل:
باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها ... جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا دعر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r4.speaker: المبرد والزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r4.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj define jadhwa as a thick piece of firewood.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r4.anchor: المبرد والزجاج: الجذوة: القطعة الغليظة من الحطب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r5.speaker: ابن قتيبة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r5.claim: Ibn Qutayba glosses it as a piece of fire, while tafsīr also gives the gloss of an already burned stick, attributed to Muqātil.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r5.anchor: ابن قتيبة: {أو جذوة من النار} أي: قطعة منها، قال: وفي التفسير: الجذوة: عود قد احترق (¬2)؛ قاله مقاتل

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says it is a piece of wood containing fire.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r7.speaker: مجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r7.claim: Mujāhid glosses jadhwa as a tree’s base or root.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r8.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r8.claim: Qatāda says it is the base of a tree with fire at its tip.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r9.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v17p381/r9.claim: Al-Kalbī interprets it as a flame of fire.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:29-30/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:29-30/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:28:29-30/r1.claim: The prior passage explains Moses completing the term; a glowing coal is a piece and flame from a fire.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says Moses completed the better and more generous of the two terms, the ten years.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: قضى أوفاهما وأبرهما

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r4.claim: Moses completed the term he had agreed to fulfill.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r5.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r5.claim: Mujahid says Moses completed ten years, stayed ten more, and left after twenty years.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589/r5.anchor: قضى العشر السنين ثم أقام بعد ذلك عشر سنين

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r1.claim: Moses perceived what seemed to be fire, though it was actually light; it appeared to him as fire.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r1.anchor: أي: رأى نارا، وإنما كان نورا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r2.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r2.claim: Moses saw fire on the mountain while off the road and told his family to wait as he sought news of the road.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p589#2/r3.claim: A glowing coal is the base of a tree; Moses hoped they could warm themselves because it was winter.

ELMALILI:28:29/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:29/r1.claim: Although the verse seems vague about which term Moses fulfilled, Elmalılı infers he completed more than required and had no term left; a noble person keeps his promise.
ELMALILI:28:29/r1.anchor: düşünülünce fazlasını ödediği ve hiçbir eceli kalmadığı anlaşılır. Çünkü kerîm olan vaadine vefâ eder

ELMALILI:28:29/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r2.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:28:29/r2.claim: Some reports say Moses remained ten years beyond the agreed period.
ELMALILI:28:29/r2.anchor: Hatta bazılarında on sene daha fazla kaldığı rivayet edilmiştir

ELMALILI:28:29/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r3.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:28:29/r3.claim: Some say Moses was heading to Egypt, though Elmalılı considers this at odds with his earlier fear that they would kill him.
ELMALILI:28:29/r3.anchor: bazıları Mısır’a demişler lâkin فَأَخَافُ أَن يَقْتُلُونِ demesi buna münâfî görünür

ELMALILI:28:29/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r4.speaker: bazıları
ELMALILI:28:29/r4.claim: Others say he headed toward Jerusalem; Elmalılı finds this safer and more apt.

ELMALILI:28:29/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:29/r5.claim: Elmalılı says ānasa conveys a deep, humanly intimate perception rather than crude sensing; he compares its use for recognizing maturity in 4:6.
ELMALILI:28:29/r5.anchor: bir ihsas ifade etmekle beraber, kaba bir ihsâsın değil, üns ifade eden derin ve insânî bir ihsâsın ifadesidir

ELMALILI:28:29/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:29/r6.claim: The indefinite tanwin on nāran carries further strange and wondrous implications.
ELMALILI:28:29/r6.anchor: نَارًۭا’daki tenvînin tenkîrindeki garâib ve acâiblik de öyle

ELMALILI:28:29/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:29/r7.claim: Moses's hope of bringing news suggests the travelers were in a difficult situation and needed information on the road.
ELMALILI:28:29/r7.anchor: demek ki yolda bir haber almaya muhtaç sıkıntılı bir vaziyette bulunuyorlardı

ELMALILI:28:29/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:29/r8.claim: One account places the family traveling in winter through unfamiliar routes, with Moses avoiding Syrian rulers; his pregnant wife and party reached Sinai's right or western side on a dark, cold, snowy night.
ELMALILI:28:29/r8.anchor: Kış mevsimi ehliyle, malıyla çıkmış ve Şam mülûkünden hazeren yolun gayrısını tutmuştu

ELMALILI:28:29/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:29/r9.claim: Another account says Moses traveled at night to rejoin his companions, lost the way, and his wife went into labor; when his flint failed, he saw a distant fire and told them to wait.
ELMALILI:28:29/r9.anchor: Haremine gayretinden geceleyin refikleriyle buluşur, gündüz ayrılırdı. Derken bir gün yolu şaşırdı, gece geldi çattı

ELMALILI:28:29/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:28:29/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:28:29/r10.claim: Elmalılı renders jadwa as an "eksi" from the fire in his Turkish translation.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r1.speaker: müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r1.claim: Although the Qur'an does not specify whether Moses completed eight or ten years with his father-in-law, exegetes say he completed ten, citing reports and prophets' fidelity to covenants.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r1.anchor: müfessirler, bazı rivayetlere ve peygamberlerin “ahde vefa” ilkesine bağlılıklarına dayanarak on yılı tamamladığını söylemektedirler

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r2.claim: After completing the appointed term, Moses set out with his family toward Egypt and saw a distant fire near Mount Tur.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r2.anchor: Mûsâ, belirlenmiş olan süreyi tamamladıktan sonra ailesiyle birlikte Mısır’a gitmek üzere yola çıkmış

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r3.speaker: tefsirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r3.claim: Exegetical accounts place the event on a cold winter night when Moses had lost his way and approached the fire hoping to find someone to guide him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:28:29/r3.anchor: soğuk bir kış gecesinde ve Mûsâ’nın yolunu kaybettiği bir sırada meydana geldiği, kendisine yol gösterecek birini bulmak ümidiyle

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r1.claim: The Qur’an and Torah do not specify whether Moses completed eight or ten years of service.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r1.anchor: It is not specified either by the Qur’ ān or the Torah whether the term completed was eight years or ten.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r2.claim: The Torah indicates Moses traveled with his wife and two children to the mount of Ṭūr on a dark, cold night.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p537/r2.anchor: with his two children besides his wife, when they reached the mount of Ṭūr, the night was dark and it was cold too.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p538/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p538/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p538/r1.claim: In darkness, Moses saw a light on the mountain and asked his family to wait while he sought people for directions or an ember for warmth.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p538/r1.anchor: he saw something shining from the side of the mount of Ṭūr. He told his wife and children to stay there

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r1.speaker: author
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir, Nafi, Abu Amr, Ibn Amir, and Kisai read جذوة with kasra; Asim alone uses fatḥa and Hamza uses ḍamma.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r1.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي: (أو جذوة) بكسر الجيم.

FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r2.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r2.claim: Abu Ubayda says جذوة is like جذمة: a thick piece of wood without flame; Ibn Muqbil's verse illustrates the word, and Abu Ubayda mentions the kasra form.
FARISI-HUJJA:v5p413/r2.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: الجذوة مثل الجذمة وهي: القطعة الغليظة من الخشب ليس فيها لهب

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r1.claim: جذوة has dialectal kasra, fatḥa, and damma forms, with kasra the most eloquent; it means a piece of wood with fire at its end.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r1.anchor: والكسر أفصح ومعنى الجذوة عود في رأسه نار

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r2.claim: الرهب may mean fear; Moses feared the staff after it became a serpent, so he was told to press his hand to his ribs to calm himself.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r2.anchor: فقيل هن لغات ومعناهن الفزع والجناح من الإنسان اليد

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r3.claim: An alternative gloss takes الرهب to mean a sleeve or pocket; on that reading its hāʾ need not be quiescent, since Arabic can reduce originally rounded or fronted vowels.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p277/r3.anchor: وقيل الرهب ها هنا الكم تقول العرب أعطني ما في رهبتك

IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.speaker: حمزة، ابن سعدان عن إسحق المسيبي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.claim: They read لأهله امكثوا with ḍamma on hāʾ in both 20:10 and 28:29; the others use kasra.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p416/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة وابن سعدان عن إسحق المسيبى ﴿ لأهله امكثوا ﴾

QIRAAT-ER:28:29:17#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:17#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:17#1/r1.claim: In li-ahlihu the pronoun suffix shifts from kasra to ḍamma, a minor phonetic variant of the third-person masculine pronoun.
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:17#1/r1.anchor: Hū-iḍāfa variant: the pronoun suffix vowel shifts from -i (standard harmony after kasra) to -u

QIRAAT-ER:28:29:18#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:18#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:18#1/r1.claim: This bundled entry links the preceding pronoun-vowel shift to the juncture with the imperative's hamzat al-waṣl.
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:18#1/r1.anchor: Same vhr entry in bundle — the preceding pronoun's vowel shift affects the juncture

QIRAAT-ER:28:29:19#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:19#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:19#1/r1.claim: The first-person possessive yāʾ in inniya takes fatḥa instead of sukūn, a prosodic variant with identical meaning.
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:19#1/r1.anchor: Y-iḍāfa variant: the 1st-sg pronoun yāʾ takes fatḥa instead of sukūn

QIRAAT-ER:28:29:22#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:22#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:22#1/r1.claim: The yāʾ in laʿalliya takes fatḥa, parallel to the same yāʾ-fatḥa pattern in inniya, with no semantic shift.

QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#1/r1.claim: Judhwatin has damma on the first radical, an alternate vocalization of jadhwa; the source says dictionaries attest all three vowels.
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#1/r1.anchor: Vowel variant: damma on the first radical — judhwa alternative form of jadhwa

QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#2/r1.claim: Jidhwatin has kasra on the first radical and is listed as a synonym of jadhwa, with a slight nuance toward a stump.
QIRAAT-ER:28:29:28#2/r1.anchor: Vowel variant: kasra on the first radical — jidhwa variant; classical dictionaries list as synonym

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r1.speaker: الكلبي
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r1.claim: Al-Kalbi explains a firebrand as a flame from the fire.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r1.anchor: عن الكلبي في قوله تعالى ﴿ جذوة من النار ﴾ قال شعلة من النار

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r2.claim: Qatada explains it as a piece of the tree with fire at its end.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p90#6/r2.anchor: وقال قتادة أصل الشجرة في طرفها النار قال فذلك قوله ﴿ جذوة من النار ﴿

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r4.claim: A prophetic report says Moses fulfilled the longer term, ten years.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r4.anchor: جاء على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه وفى أطول الأجلين، وهو العشر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r5.claim: Mujahid says Moses fulfilled ten years or ten with an additional period; the author judges the second report weak.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد: وفي عشر أو عشرا بعدها، وهذا ضعيف

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r6.claim: Moses travelled with his household toward Egypt, his homeland and the land of his people; exegetes disagree whether he married the elder or younger daughter and about her name.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r6.anchor: وسار بأهله: أي نحو مصر بلده وبلد قومه. والخلاف فيمن تزوج، الكبرى أم الصغرى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r7.claim: The journey and the fire were discussed earlier in Surat Taha and elsewhere.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r7.anchor: وتقدم كيفية مسيره، وإيناسه النار في سورة طه وغيرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r8.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r8.claim: The majority read جذوة with kasra; al-A'mash, Talha, Abu Haywa, and Hamza use damma, while Asim except al-Ja'fi uses fatha.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r8.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: جذوة، بكسر الجيم والأعمش، وطلحة، وأبو حيوة، وحمزة: بضمها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r9.claim: تصطلون means warming yourselves: it was a cold night and they had lost the road.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p301/r9.anchor: لعلكم تصطلون: أي تتسخنون بها، إذ كانت ليلة باردة، وقد أضلوا الطريق

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r1.claim: Musa completed the term agreed with Shuayb, and the author takes it to be the latter term, citing Ibn Mardawayh from Muqsim through al-Hasan ibn Ali.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r1.anchor: أي أتم المدة المضروبة لما أراد شعيب منه والمراد به الأجل الآخر

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says Musa fulfilled the longer and better of the two terms, because God's Messenger keeps his word; Bukhari and others transmit this answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه سئل أي الأجلين قضى موسى عليه السلام فقال : قضى أكثرهما وأطيبهما

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r3.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r3.claim: A report through Abu Sa'id says that after the Prophet and successive angels each defer the answer, God declares that Musa fulfilled the more complete and better term, ten years; the author gives the extended chain but no grading.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r3.anchor: عن أبي سعيد الخدري أن رجلا سأله أي الأجلين قضى موسى

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r4.claim: The fāʾ is resumptive: he made the two contracts, undertook the work, and when he completed the term, set out with his family.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r4.anchor: فصيحة أي فعقد العقدين وباشر موسى ما أريد منه فلما أتم الاجل

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r5.claim: One view has Musa travel toward Egypt, with Shuayb's permission, to visit his mother, brother, sister, and relatives because the long absence made him think the old case forgotten; another has him go toward Jerusalem, which the author considers less likely.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r5.anchor: قيل : نحو مصر باذن من شعيب عليه السلام لزيارة والدته وأخيه

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r6.claim: Anisa originally means perception and is broader than sight; al-Zamakhshari defines it as clear, unambiguous seeing, linking humans to visibility and jinn to concealment, while another view means seeing what is comforting.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r6.anchor: وأصل الايناس على ما قيل الاحساس فيكون أعم من الابصار

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r7.claim: Some mystics say what Musa saw was real light, called fire because he thought it was fire; others say it had the appearance of actual fire but its reality lay beyond reason.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r7.anchor: استظهر بعضهم أن المبصر كان نورا حقيقيا إلا أنه عبر عنه بالنار

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r8.claim: His family may have been wife and servant, or wife and two sons Gershom and Eliezer born during his stay; the latter requires additional years after the contract if he did not consummate the marriage until afterward.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r8.anchor: كان معه عليه السلام على قول امرأته وخادم ويخاطب الاثنان بصيغة الجمع

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r9.speaker: وهب
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r9.claim: Wahb says Musa's child was born on the road on the night he noticed the fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r9.anchor: وعن وهب أنه عليه السلام ولد له ولد في الطريق ليلة إيناس النار

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r10.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r10.claim: Abu Hayyan describes a winter journey on an unfamiliar route to avoid Syrian rulers, with Musa's pregnant wife unsure when she would deliver; his jealousy made them alternate between the caravan at night and separation by day, and after losing the route in a dark, freezing, snowy night she went into labor, his flint failed, and they saw a distant fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r10.anchor: أنه عليه السلام خرج بأهله وماله في فصل الشتاء وأخذ على غير الطريق

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r11.claim: He promises news about the road because the family had lost their way; the sentence explains why he tells them to wait.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r11.anchor: بخبر ( أي بخبر الطريق بأن أجد عندها من يخبرني به

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r12.claim: Jadwah may be a thick piece of wood with fire at its end or without it, as illustrated by two poems; God's words from the fire clarify the kind meant and intensify it by treating the brand as fire itself.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r12.anchor: أي عود غليظ سواء كان في رأسه نار كما في قوله

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r13.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r13.claim: Al-Raghib defines a jadwah as what remains of wood after it has burned.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r13.anchor: وقال الراغب : الجذوة ما يبقى من الحطب بعد الالتهاب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r14.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r14.claim: Abu Hayyan defines it as a piece of wood containing fire but without a flame.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r14.anchor: وفي معناه قول أبي حيان : عود فيه نار بلا لهب

ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r15.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r15.claim: Ibn Zayd says it is a stick of wood containing fire.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p71/r15.anchor: عن أبن زيد قال : هي عود من حطب فيه النار

ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r1.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r1.claim: Qatada says the jadwah was the base of a tree with fire at its tip; on this reading min marks the source, and the fire is the one Musa had already noticed.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r1.anchor: عن قتادة أنها أصل شجرة في طرفها النار قيل : فتكون من على هذا للابتداء

ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r2.claim: Most readers pronounce jadwah with kasra on jīm; al-A'mash, Talha, Abu Haywa, and Hamza use damma.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r2.anchor: وقرأ الأكثر ( جذوة ) بكسر الجيم والاعمش وطلحة وأبو حيوة وحمزة بضمها

ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r3.claim: Taṣṭalūn means that they warm themselves, proving they were suffering from cold.
ALUSI-FULL:v20p72/r3.anchor: تستدفئون وتتسخنون بها وفيه دليل على أنهم أصابهم برد

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r1.claim: Moses completed the appointed term fully and finished it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r1.anchor: قضى موسى الأجل} يعني أتمه وفرغ منه،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r2.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r2.claim: Mujahid says Moses stayed another ten years with his father-in-law after finishing the term, making twenty years in all, then sought and received permission to return to Egypt.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r2.anchor: قال مجاهد: لما قضى موسى الأجل مكث بعد ذلك عند صهره عشرا آخر فأقام عنده عشرين سنة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r3.claim: Moses traveled through a dark, intensely cold wilderness night while his wife went into labor.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r3.anchor: وكان في البرية في ليلة مظلمة، شديدة البرد وأخذ امرأته الطلق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r4.claim: Anasa means saw; Moses had lost the road and hoped to bring back news of it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r4.anchor:
لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر}
عن الطريق، لأنه كان قد أخطأ الطريق،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r5.claim: A jadhwa is a piece or flame of fire; three vowel readings are reported: Asim opens jīm, Hamza dammas it, and the others kasra it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r5.anchor: {أو جذوة من النار} يعني: قطعة وشعلة من النار. وفيها ثلاث لغات، قرأ عاصم: "جذوة" بفتح الجيم،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r6.claim: Qatada and Muqatil explain the jadhwa as a stick partly burned; its plural is judha.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r6.anchor: قال قتادة ومقاتل: هي العود الذي قد احترق بعضه، وجمعها "جذى"

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p205#2/r7.claim: Taṣṭalun means that they might warm themselves.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r1.claim: Moses completed the term and traveled with his wife; a report says he completed the longer term, served ten more years, then chose to return.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r1.anchor: بامرأته. روي أنه قضى أقصى الأجلين ومكث بعد ذلك عنده عشرا أخرى ثم عزم على الرجوع.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r2.claim: He saw fire from the side facing the mountain and asked his family to wait while he sought news of the route; jadhwah is a thick stick whether burning or not.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r2.anchor: بخبر الطريق. { أو جذوة } عود غليظ سواء كان في رأسه نار أو لم يكن.

BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r3.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r3.claim: Two poems illustrate a large firewood stick and a firebrand; Asim reads jadhwah with fatḥa, Hamza with ḍamma, and both are dialectal forms.
BAYDAWI-FULL:28:29-30/r3.anchor: وقال آخر: وألقى على قبس من النار جذوة شديدا عليه حرها والتهابها ولذلك بينه بقوله: { من النار }

BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r1.claim: The passage quotes the Torah's account that Jacob's twelve sons entered Egypt, numbering seventy including Joseph, and that their descendants multiplied greatly after Joseph and his generation died.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r1.anchor: ذكر المضمون هذا من التوراة : قال في و السفر الثاني منها

BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r2.claim: A new Pharaoh, unaware of Joseph, feared Israel's growth and imposed harsh forced labor, using them to build store cities including Pithom and Raamses.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r2.anchor: فملك على مصر ملك جديد لم يكن يعرفيوسف

BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r3.claim: Pharaoh ordered Hebrew midwives Puah and Shiphrah to kill newborn boys and spare girls; they feared God, disobeyed, and said Hebrew women gave birth before a midwife arrived.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r3.anchor: التي تسمى إحداهما فوعا والخرى شوفرا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r4.claim: The Torah says God treated the midwives well and gave them households; Pharaoh then ordered every Hebrew boy thrown in the river while girls were spared.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r4.anchor: فأحسن اله إلى القابلتين لصنعهما هذا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r5.claim: A Levite couple hid their attractive newborn son for three months, then placed him in a pitch-coated wooden basket in the river shallows while his sister watched.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r5.anchor: فأخذت تابوتا من خشب الصنوبر , وطلته بالقار والزفت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r6.claim: Pharaoh's daughter found the crying child while bathing, felt compassion, and drew him from the water.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p480/r6.anchor: فخرجت بنت فرعون تغتسل في النهر , فنظرت إلى التابوت

BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r1.claim: The Torah account says the child's sister arranged for his mother to nurse him for Pharaoh's daughter; later the princess adopted and named him Moses because she drew him from water.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r1.anchor: فأخذت المرأة الغلام فأرضعته فشب الغلام فأتت به

BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r2.claim: As an adult Moses killed an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, then the next day rebuked a Hebrew disputant, who exposed the killing; Pharaoh sought him, so Moses fled to Midian.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r2.anchor: فقتل المصري , فمات ودفنه في الرمل

BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r3.claim: At Midian Moses rescued and watered the seven daughters of Reuel, was invited to eat, married Zipporah, and had a son named Eliezer.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r4.claim: The claim that both disputants were Hebrews should be aligned with the Qur'an if possible; otherwise the Torah account was altered.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r4.anchor: إن أمكن تنزيل ما في القرآن عليه فذاك , وإلا فهو مما بدلوه

BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r5.claim: Al-Zamakhshari supports the Torah's statement that Shuʿayb had seven daughters by identifying the two women in the Qur'anic account, though the author says that identification is not necessary.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r6.claim: Moses completed the full agreed term and fulfilled all the work he had promised his father-in-law.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p481/r6.anchor: أن التقدير : فلما التزم موسى عليه السلام

BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r1.speaker: أبو ذر رضي الله عنه
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r1.claim: A report raised to the Prophet and transmitted by al-Ṭabarānī from Abu Dharr says Moses completed the more complete of the two terms.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r1.anchor: روى الطبراني في الوسط معناه عن أبي ذر رضي الله عنه مرفوعا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r2.claim: Moses appears to have remained with his father-in-law after the term, since the coordinated phrase 'and he traveled' is not the direct result of 'when he completed.'

BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r3.claim: Anasa means that Moses saw the fire; its light cheered him, and he needed both directions and warmth.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r4.claim: He tells his family to stay, using the masculine plural by grammatical precedence and because sons may also have accompanied him; the wording emphasizes that women should be sheltered.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r4.anchor: ولما كان النساء أعظم ما ينبغي ستره , أطلق عليها ضمير الذكور

BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r5.claim: He emphasizes seeing a fire because a flame in a remote, cold place at that time seems unlikely.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r5.anchor: لاستبعاد أن يكون في ذلك المكان القفر وفي ذلك الوقت الشديد البرد نار

BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r6.claim: His tentative 'perhaps' expresses humility, the surah's intended quality; a thick branch with embers might provide useful directions or warmth.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r6.anchor: ولذا عبر بالجذوة التي مدار مادتها الثبات

BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r7.claim: Laʿallakum taṣṭalūn means hoping to draw near and warm themselves at the fire, indicating a winter night.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p482/r7.anchor: لتكونوا على رجاء من أن تقربوا من النار

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r1.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r1.claim: Moses completed the agreed term of ten years, then remained for another ten.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {فلما قضى موسى الأجل} قال: عشر سنينثم مكث بعد ذلك عشرا أخرى

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r2.claim: Moses set out with his family in winter after losing the way; the apparent fire was God's light, and he sought guidance or fire to warm them.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r2.anchor: من طريق السدي قال عبد الله بن عباس لما قضى موسى الأجل سار بأهله فضل عن الطريق

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r3.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r3.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله (آنس) قال: أحس وفي قوله {إني آنست نارا} قال: أحسست

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r4.claim: Moses hoped to find someone to guide him because the travelers had lost their route.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر} قال: لعلي أجد من يدلني على الطريق

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r5.claim: 'جذوة' means a flame or burning brand.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {جذوة} قال: شهاب

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r6.claim: 'جذوة' means the base of a tree.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله {جذوة} قال: أصل شجرة

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r7.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r7.claim: A 'جذوة' is a tree base with fire at its tip.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r7.anchor: عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله {جذوة} قال: أصل شجرة في طرفها نار

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r8.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r8.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال الجذوة عود من حطب فيه النار

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r9.speaker: عاصم
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r9.claim: ʿAsim recited 'أو جذوة' with fatḥa on the jīm.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r9.anchor: عن عاصم رضي الله عنه أنه قرأ (أو جذوة) بنصب الجيم

DURR-FULL:v6p411/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r10.speaker: ميمون بن مهران
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r10.claim: Maymun counsels seeking religious gain on a worldly journey: Sheba's queen found Islam when leaving her kingdom, and Moses found God's speech when seeking fire.
DURR-FULL:v6p411/r10.anchor: عن أبي المليح قال: أتيت ميمون بن مهران لا ودعه عند خروجي في تجارة فقال: لا تيأس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.speaker: الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.claim: Hasan, Ata, and Ikrima hold that all of al-Qasas is Meccan.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p198#3/r10.anchor: وروي عن الحسن وعطاء وعكرمة أنها مكية كلها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: Sibawayh conditions the construction after ḥattā on whether the entry is brought about by the journey, contrasting Zayd’s entry with sunrise and with baggage or the traveler’s body arriving.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.anchor: وذلك قولك سرت حتى يدخلها زيد إذا كان دخول زيد لم يؤده سيرك ولم يكن

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: He treats arrival of one’s baggage or body as an event brought about by the journey, and compares it with entry that the journey has led to.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.anchor: ولكنك لو قلت سرت حتى يدخلها ثقلى وسرت حتى يدخلها بدنى

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: Sibawayh permits coordinating another clause after repeated ḥattā; the second clause may be raised, as in the verse of Imruʾ al-Qays he cites.

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: With one ḥattā shared across the coordination, raising “the sun rises” is not allowed, and making it subjunctive after a raised first verb is impossible.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.anchor: واعلم أنه لا يجوز سرت حتى أدخلها وتطلع

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: Repeating ḥattā before the second clause avoids that problem, just as repeating a preposition can be good Arabic.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.anchor: ويحسن أن تقول سرت حتى تطلع الشمس وحتى أدخلها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: The coordinated “I traveled and he traveled until we enter” is understood as a joint journey, equivalent to saying “we traveled.”
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.anchor: وتقول سرت وسار حتى ندخلها كأنك قلت سرنا حتى ندخلها

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: “Until I hear the call” takes the subjunctive because the journey does not cause hearing; dawn causes it, while travel can cause exhaustion and thus permits “until I tire.”
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.anchor: حتى أسمع الأذان هذا وجهه وحده النصب

SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.author: Sībawayh
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.speaker: author
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.claim: “Until I become morning” is likewise treated as a limit caused by sunrise, not by the traveler’s movement.
SIBAWAYH:وذلكقولكسرتحتىيدخلهازيدإذاكاندخ.anchor: أصبح لأن الإصباح لا يؤديه سيرك إنما هي غاية طلوع الشمس

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r1.claim: Moses’ promise to bring news from the fire corresponds to Qasas’s closing promise that God will show signs, with a deliberate verbal echo between saʾātīkum and sayurīkum.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r1.anchor: ومناسبته لقوله تعالى في آخر السورة: {الحمد للَّهِ سَيُرِيكُمْ آيَاتِهِ فَتَعْرِفُونَهَا}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r2.claim: Naml repeats the verb of coming while Qasas uses it once; the author reads the repetition as confidence and strength, fitting Naml, and the single use as fitting Qasas’s fearful atmosphere.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r2.anchor: فأكد الإتيان في سورة النمل لقوة يقينه وثقته بنفسه، والتوكيد يدل على القوة، في حين لم يكرر فعل الإتيان في القصص مناسبة لجو الخوف.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r3.claim: The repeated wording also fits the narrative counts: the verb atā occurs twelve times in Naml and six times in Qasas.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r3.anchor: إن فعل (الإتيان) تكرر في النمل اثنتي عشرة مرة. وتكرر في القصص ست مرات فناسب تكرار {آتِيكُمْ} في النمل من كل وجه.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r4.claim: A shihāb is a bright, shining flame; a qabas is a flame taken from a larger fire, and the root also describes acquiring knowledge.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p95/r4.anchor: فذكر في سورة النمل أنه يأتيهم بشهاب قبس، والشهاب: هو شعلة من النار ساطعة. ومعنى (القَبَس) شعلة نار تقتبس من معظم النار

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p605/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p605/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p605/r1.claim: Sayr is extended travel toward a direction or purpose—here from Madyan to Egypt—while walking merely means moving and need not have a set destination; travel can serve trade or admonition.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p605/r1.anchor: السير غير المشي في اللغة ويقال سار القوم إذا امتد بهم السير من جهة إلى جهة معينة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r1.speaker: أهل اللغة
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r1.claim: Linguists say nabaʾ is more important and significant than khabar and carries an important benefit.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r1.anchor: النبأ كما يقول أهل اللغة أهم من الخبر وأعظم منه وفيه فائدة مهمة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r2.claim: Nabaʾ linguistically means emergence or becoming manifest.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r3.claim: The Qur'an uses singular khabar twice in Moses' story, but uses nabaʾ for weighty accounts of earlier peoples and messengers.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p917/r3.anchor: وقد استعمل القرآن الكريم كلمة خبر مفردة في موطنين في قصة موسى - عليه السلام -

NASHR:v1p345/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p345/r1.claim: The author endorses the preceding explanation that Arabs lengthen negation in supplication, seeking aid, and emphatic denial, even without a formal cause.
NASHR:v1p345/r1.anchor: قال: وهذا معروف عند العرب؛ لأنها تمد عند الدعاء عند الاستغاثة، وعند المبالغة في نفي شيء

NASHR:v1p345/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p345/r2.claim: He says the lengthening has two causes here, emphasis and the hamza; lengthening with a sound basis is more deserving than lengthening without one.
NASHR:v1p345/r2.anchor: يشير إلى كونه اجتمع سببان، وهما المبالغة ووجود الهمزة كما سيأتي

NASHR:v1p345/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r3.speaker: محيي الدين النووي
NASHR:v1p345/r3.claim: Al-Nawawi calls lengthening لا إله إلا الله the correct, preferred practice because it aids reflection; he says early and later authorities commonly did so.
NASHR:v1p345/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ محيي الدين النووي - رحمه الله - في " الأذكار ": ولهذا كان المذهب الصحيح المختار

NASHR:v1p345/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p345/r4.claim: The author cites two raised reports: Ibn Umar is promised the Abode of Majesty and vision of God, while Anas is promised the erasure of four thousand sins; both reports are weak but used for devotional virtues.
NASHR:v1p345/r4.anchor: روينا في ذلك حديثين مرفوعين أحدهما عن ابن عمر

NASHR:v1p345/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r5.speaker: حمزة
NASHR:v1p345/r5.claim: Hamza prolongs emphatic lā in several negative formulas; Ibn Sawwar, Sibt al-Khayyat, Ibn Faris, and al-Khuza'i transmit the reading through multiple Hamza routes.
NASHR:v1p345/r5.anchor: مد المبالغة للنفي في (لا) التي للتبرئة في نحو (لا ريب فيه) ، (لا شية فيها) ، (لا مرد له) ، (لا جرم) ، عن حمزة

NASHR:v1p345/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r6.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p345/r6.claim: The author documents the emphatic-lā reading through Ibn Sawwar, Sibt al-Khayyat, Ibn Faris, and al-Khuza'i, including reports through Khalaf, Sulaym, Khallad, and others.
NASHR:v1p345/r6.anchor: نص على ذلك له أبو طاهر بن سوار

NASHR:v1p345/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r7.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p345/r7.claim: The author reads this lengthening at a moderate degree, short of full prolongation, because its cause is weaker than the cause of hamza.
NASHR:v1p345/r7.anchor: وقدَر المد في ذلك فيما قرأنا به وسط لا يبلغ الإشباع، وكذا نص عليه الأستاذ أبو عبد الله بن القصاع

NASHR:v1p345/r8.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p345/r8.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p345/r8.claim: He also reads lengthening in لا ريب alone for Hafs through Hubayra, as reported in al-Kifaya for the six readings.
NASHR:v1p345/r8.anchor: وقرأت بالمد أيضا في (لا ريب) فقط

ITQAN:v2p325#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p325#2/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p325#2/r1.claim: جذوة means a flame or firebrand.

ITQAN:v1p193/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p193/r1.claim: The author rejects heretical use of Anas's report as proof that only four companions memorized the Qur’an: collective tawātur can cover it through distributed memorization.
ITQAN:v1p193/r1.anchor: ولا متمسك لهم فيه فإنا لا نسلم حمله على ظاهره سلمناه ولكن من أين لهم

ITQAN:v1p193/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r2.speaker: القرطبي
ITQAN:v1p193/r2.claim: Al-Qurṭubī says Anas named those four because of his special attachment to them or because they came to mind, not to exclude others.
ITQAN:v1p193/r2.anchor: وقال القرطبي قد قتل يوم اليمامة سبعون من القراء وقتل في عهد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

ITQAN:v1p193/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r3.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r3.claim: Al-Bāqillānī's first answer is that Anas's wording does not imply nobody else collected the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v1p193/r3.anchor: أحدها أنه لا مفهوم له فلا يلزم ألا يكون غيرهم جمعه

ITQAN:v1p193/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r4.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r4.claim: His second answer is that only those four collected all the revealed readings and modes.
ITQAN:v1p193/r4.anchor: الثاني المراد لم يجمعه على جميع الوجوه والقراءات التي نزل بها إلا أولئك

ITQAN:v1p193/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r5.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r5.claim: His third answer is that only those four collected both recitation later abrogated and recitation that remained.
ITQAN:v1p193/r5.anchor: الثالث لم يجمع ما نسخ منه بعد تلاوته وما لم ينسخ إلا أولئك

ITQAN:v1p193/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r6.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r6.claim: His fourth answer limits collection to direct reception from the Prophet; others may have received some portions through intermediaries.
ITQAN:v1p193/r6.anchor: الرابع أن المراد بجمعه تلقيه من في رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لا بواسطة

ITQAN:v1p193/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r7.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r7.claim: His fifth answer is that the four were publicly known for teaching and recitation, while Anas did not know the status of others.
ITQAN:v1p193/r7.anchor: الخامس أنهم تصدوا لإلقائه وتعليمه فاشتهروا به وخفي حال غيرهم

ITQAN:v1p193/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r8.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r8.claim: His sixth answer takes collection as writing: this does not deny that others memorized it, while the four did both.
ITQAN:v1p193/r8.anchor: السادس المراد بالجمع الكتابة فلا ينفي أن يكون غيرهم جمعه حفظا عن ظهر قلبه

ITQAN:v1p193/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r9.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r9.claim: His seventh answer is that only the four explicitly completed memorization during the Prophet's life; others may have finished when the final verse arrived.
ITQAN:v1p193/r9.anchor: السابع المراد أن أحدا لم يفصح بأنه جمعه بمعنى أكمل حفظه في عهد رسول الله

ITQAN:v1p193/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r10.speaker: القاضي أبو بكر الباقلاني
ITQAN:v1p193/r10.claim: His eighth answer understands collection as hearing, obeying, and acting on the Qur’an.
ITQAN:v1p193/r10.anchor: الثامن أن المراد بجمعه السمع والطاعة له والعمل بموجبه

ITQAN:v1p193/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p193/r11.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ITQAN:v1p193/r11.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda says the true collector of the Qur’an is one who hears and obeys it, in response to a man saying his son had collected it.
ITQAN:v1p193/r11.anchor: أبا الدرداء فقال إن إبني جمع القرآن فقال اللهم غفرا إنما جمع القرآن من سمع له

ITQAN:v4p405/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r1.speaker: غيره
ITQAN:v4p405/r1.claim: An unnamed explanation says whoever collects the Qur’an yet enters the Fire is worse than a pig.
ITQAN:v4p405/r1.anchor: وقال ( غيره ) معناه من جمع القرآن ثم دخل النار فهو شر من الخنزير

ITQAN:v4p405/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r2.speaker: ابن الأنباري
ITQAN:v4p405/r2.claim: Ibn al-Anbārī says the Fire cannot erase Qur’an from memorizing hearts, like water cannot wash the revealed Book from its pure repositories.
ITQAN:v4p405/r2.anchor: وقال ابن الأنباري معناه أن النار لا تبطله ولا تقلعه من الأسماع التي وعته

ITQAN:v4p405/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r3.speaker: عصمة بن مالك
ITQAN:v4p405/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports from ʿIṣma b. Mālik: if the Qur’an were placed in a hide, the Fire would not burn it.
ITQAN:v4p405/r3.anchor: وعند الطبراني من حديث عصمة بن مالك ( لو جمع القرآن في إهاب ما أحرقته النار )

ITQAN:v4p405/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r4.speaker: سهل بن سعد
ITQAN:v4p405/r4.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī reports from Sahl b. Saʿd: if the Qur’an were in a hide, the Fire would not touch it.
ITQAN:v4p405/r4.anchor: وعنده من حديث سهل بن سعد ( لو كان القرآن في إهاب ما مسته النار )

ITQAN:v4p405/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r5.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v4p405/r5.claim: Anas reports that one who reads Qur’an day and night and follows its lawful and forbidden rulings is protected from Fire, joined to the noble scribes, and aided by Qur’an at Judgment.
ITQAN:v4p405/r5.anchor: من قرأ القرآن يقوم به آناء الليل والنهار يحل حلاله ويحرم حرامه حرم الله لحمه ودمه على النار

ITQAN:v4p405/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r6.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v4p405/r6.claim: Anas reports that Qur’an is an accepted intercessor and confirming witness: following it leads to Paradise, leaving it behind leads to Fire.
ITQAN:v4p405/r6.anchor: وأخرج أبو عبيد عن أنس مرفوعا ( القرآن شافع مشفع وماجد مصدق من جعله إمامه

ITQAN:v4p405/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r7.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v4p405/r7.claim: Anas reports that the bearers of Qur’an are leaders or notable people of Paradise.
ITQAN:v4p405/r7.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني من حديث أنس ( حملة القرآن عرفاء أهل الجنة )

ITQAN:v4p405/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r8.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v4p405/r8.claim: Anas reports that the people of Qur’an are God’s own people and special elect.
ITQAN:v4p405/r8.anchor: وأخرج النسائي وابن ماجه والحاكم من حديث أنس قال ( أهل القرآن هم أهل الله وخاصته )

ITQAN:v4p405/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r9.speaker: أبو هريرة
ITQAN:v4p405/r9.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that three Qur’anic verses recited in prayer are better than three large pregnant camels.
ITQAN:v4p405/r9.anchor: وأخرج مسلم وغيره من حديث أبي هريرة أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال ( أيحب أحدكم

ITQAN:v4p405/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r10.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
ITQAN:v4p405/r10.claim: Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh reports the Prophet saying that the best speech is God’s Book.
ITQAN:v4p405/r10.anchor: وأخرج مسلم من حديث جابر بن عبد الله ( خير الحديث كتاب الله )

ITQAN:v4p405/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r11.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
ITQAN:v4p405/r11.claim: Muʿādh b. Anas reports that one who recites the Qur’an in God’s cause is counted with the truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
ITQAN:v4p405/r11.anchor: وأخرج أحمد من حديث معاذ بن أنس ( من قرأ القرآن في سبيل الله كتب مع الصديقين

ITQAN:v4p405/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r12.speaker: أبو هريرة
ITQAN:v4p405/r12.claim: Abu Hurayra reports that teaching one’s child the Qur’an brings the parent a crown in Paradise on Judgment Day.
ITQAN:v4p405/r12.anchor: وأخرج الطبراني في الأوسط من حديث أبي هريرة ( ما من رجل يعلم ولده القرآن إلا توج

ITQAN:v4p405/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v4p405/r13.speaker: معاذ بن أنس
ITQAN:v4p405/r13.claim: Muʿādh b. Anas reports that a parent of one who completes and practices the Qur’an wears a crown brighter than the sun; the reward of the practitioner is greater.
ITQAN:v4p405/r13.anchor: وأخرج أبو داود وأحمد والحاكم من حديث معاذ بن أنس ( من قرأ القرآن فأكمله وعمل به

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.claim: Moses’ promise in al-Naml is firmer than his hope in al-Qaṣaṣ, and a blazing brand is harder to bring than an ember.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p105/r1.anchor: فقط قطع في النمل على نفسه أن يأتيهم بخبرٍ أو شهابٍ قبس، في حين ترجّى ذلك في القصص. والقطع أشق وأصعب من الترجي

BURHAN:v3p27/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.claim: Repeated tellings of Moses and Pharaoh differ in wording, order, and detail because each version carries a nuance found only there; unlike earlier scripture's separate single tellings, Joseph's story is collected in one sura.
BURHAN:v3p27/r2.anchor: فقد يوجد في ألفاظها زيادة ونقصان وتقديم وتأخير

DAMGHANI:v1p54/r6.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r6.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r6.claim: أهل can mean one's wife and children.
DAMGHANI:v1p54/r6.anchor: الرابع : الأهل يعني الزوجة والأولاد . قوله تعالى في سورة القصص

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r7.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r7.claim: Ahl can refer to a wife, as in Moses travelling with his family.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p163#2/r7.anchor: والرابع : الزوجة . ومنه قوله تعالى في القصص

SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.claim: The parallel accounts of Moses finding a fire vary in wording: al-Naml mentions a firebrand, while al-Qasas says a firewood ember and includes his instruction to wait.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR-MUH:p99/r3.anchor: سآتيكم منها بخبر أو آتيكم بشهاب قبس لعلكم تصطلون

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.claim: The Naml account says Musa perceived a fire; al-Qaṣaṣ adds that it was from the side of the mountain.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r1.anchor: النمل القصص {إني آنَسْتُ نَاراً} {آنَسَ مِن جَانِبِ الطور نَاراً}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r2.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds Musa's instruction for his family to stay while he goes to the fire; the comparison lists this detail as absent from Naml.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r3.claim: Naml uses a definite promise that Musa will bring news, while al-Qaṣaṣ phrases it as a hope or possibility.

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.claim: The Naml wording specifies a burning brand, while al-Qaṣaṣ speaks more generally of a firebrand.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p91/r4.anchor: {أَوْ آتِيكُمْ بِشِهَابٍ قَبَسٍ} {أَوْ جَذْوَةٍ مِّنَ النار}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.claim: The more specific idkhāl pairs with the more specific shihāb qabas, while the broader sulūk pairs with the broader jadwah.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p112/r3.anchor: وناسب أن يوضع الإدخال، وهو أخص من السلوك مع (الشهاب القبس) الذي هو أخَصُّ من الجذوة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds the location on the mountain's side because that sūra develops the scene in greater detail.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r2.anchor: فزاد {مِن جَانِبِ الطور} وذلك لمقامِ التفصيلِ الذي بُنيت عليه القصة في سورة القصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.claim: Al-Qaṣaṣ adds Musa's instruction to his family to stay, another detail suited to its expanded narrative rather than Naml's concise account.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r3.anchor: بزيادة {امكثوا} . وهذه الزيادة نظيرة ما ذكرناه آنفاً أعني مناسبة لمقامِ التفصيل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.claim: Musa's fear in al-Qaṣaṣ makes his promise tentative (perhaps he will bring news); Naml's less fearful, confident scene uses the definite promise that he will return.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT:p93/r4.anchor: فبنى الكلام في النمل على القطع {سَآتِيكُمْ} وفي القصص على الترجي {لعلي آتِيكُمْ}

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.claim: Qasas adds the location من جانب الطور because its retelling favors detail, unlike the concise Naml account.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r2.anchor: وذلك لمقام التفصيل الذي بنيت عليه القصة في سورة القصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.claim: Qasas also adds امكثوا, another detail suited to its expanded telling, whereas the Naml story is built on brevity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r3.anchor: بزيادة "امْكُثُوا". وهذه الزيادة نظيرة ما ذكرناه آنفا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.claim: Naml’s certain سآتيكم fits the absence of fear there and the honor shown Moses; Qasas’s hopeful لعلي آتيكم fits a frightened speaker unable to promise what will happen.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p72/r4.anchor: وذلك أن مقام الخوف في القصص لم يدعه يقطع بالأمر فإن الخائف لا يستطيع القطع بما سيفعل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.claim: He introduces Musa’s story in Naml and Qasas as another broad narrative comparison, to be studied through its many similarities and differences.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p549/r3.anchor: ومثال آخر على التشابه والاختلاف في القرآن الكريم ما جاء في سورتي النمل والقصص

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.claim: Al-Qasas uses expressions of hope in ten places, while al-Naml has only two; the author says hope marks al-Qasas and certainty marks al-Naml.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r1.anchor: الترجي من سمات سورة القصص، والقطع من سمات سورة النمل

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p73/r3.claim: Moses' promise to bring news harmonizes with the sura's closing promise that God will show signs, linking سآتيكم with سيريكم.

IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r4.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائي
IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r4.claim: These readers use kasra on jīm in جذوة; ʿĀṣim uses fatḥa and Hamza ḍamma.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p492/r4.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وأبو عمرو والكسائى ﴿ جذوة ﴾ بكسر الجيم وقرأ عاصم

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.speaker: نافع
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.claim: Of twelve disputed possessive yāʾs, Nafi opens all except معي ردءا, which he leaves quiescent.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r2.anchor: ففتحهن نافع إلا قوله ﴿ معي ردءا ﴾ فإنه أسكنها

IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.author: Ibn Mujāhid
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr open nine listed possessive yāʾs and leave quiescent إني أريد, ستجدني إن شاء الله, and معي ردءا.
IBNMUJAHID:v1p495/r3.anchor: وفتح ابن كثير تسع آيات منهن وأسكن ﴿ إني أريد ﴾ و ﴿ ستجدني إن شاء الله ﴾

NASHR:v2p165/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p165/r3.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو جعفر
NASHR:v2p165/r3.claim: Nafiʿ, Ibn Kathir, Abu ʿAmr, Ibn ʿAmir, and Abu Jaʿfar use fatḥ on the final ya of لعلي in six occurrences across Yusuf, Taha, al-Muʾminun, al-Qasas, and Ghafir.
NASHR:v2p165/r3.anchor: واتفق نافع وابن كثير وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وأبو جعفر على فتح لعلي حيث وقعت

NASHR:v2p165/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p165/r5.speaker: الهذلي
NASHR:v2p165/r5.claim: Al-Hudhali uniquely reports sukūn in the two al-Qasas locations from Ibn Dhakwan through al-Suri, and also reports sukūn in the Taha location from Zayd.
NASHR:v2p165/r5.anchor: وانفرد الهذلي عن الشذائي عن الرملي عن الصوري عن ابن ذكوان بإسكان موضعي القصص

NASHR:v2p341/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p341/r5.speaker: عاصم وحمزة وخلف
NASHR:v2p341/r5.claim: ʿĀṣim reads the initial jīm with fatḥa, Ḥamza and Khalaf with ḍamma, and the remaining readers with kasra.
NASHR:v2p341/r5.anchor: جذوة فقرأ عاصم بفتح الجيم، وقرأ حمزة وخلف بضمها،

NASHR:v2p342/r6.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r6.speaker: المدنيان وابن كثير وأبو عمرو
NASHR:v2p342/r6.claim: The two Medinans, Ibn Kathīr, and Abū ʿAmr open six first-person yāʾs in the listed Qasas phrases, including ربي إني, إني آنست, إني أنا الله, إني أخاف, and two occurrences of ربي أعلم.
NASHR:v2p342/r6.anchor: ربي أن إني آنست إني أنا الله إني أخاف ربي أعلم موضعان، فتح الست المدنيان

NASHR:v2p342/r7.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p342/r7.speaker: يعقوب والكوفيون
NASHR:v2p342/r7.claim: Yaʿqūb and the Kufans make the yāʾ still in both occurrences of لعلي.
NASHR:v2p342/r7.anchor: لعلي موضعان أسكنها فيهما يعقوب، والكوفيون،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r3.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r3.claim: Al-Farrāʾ explains the root jadhā as cutting off; a jadhwa is wood with fire but no flame.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r3.anchor: وقال الفراء: حبس جذوت الشيء جذوا: قطعته، والجذوة: عود فيه نار بلا لهب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r4.speaker: ابن مقبل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r4.claim: Ibn Muqbil's verse describes large, sturdy firewood; khawār is wood that breaks apart, and dhaʿr is worn or tired wood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r4.anchor: قال ابن مقبل: باتت حواطب ليلى يلتمسن لها ... جزل الجذا غير خوار ولا ذعر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r5.claim: An unnamed poet uses jadhwa for an ember taken from a fire and describes its remaining heat and blaze.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r5.anchor: وقال آخر: وألقى على قبس من النار جذوة ... عليها حمثها والتهابها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r6.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r6.claim: Al-Sulamī says jadhwa has three possible vowels on its jīm and means a thick stick, burning or not.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r6.anchor: وقيل: الجذوة مثلث الجيم، العود الغليظ، كانت في رأسه نار أو لم تكن

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r7.speaker: السلمي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r7.claim: Al-Sulamī's verse uses al-jadhā for firewood while describing hardship for an old man.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p278#5/r7.anchor: وقال السلمي يصف الصلى: حمى حب هذي النار حب خليلتي ... وحب الغواني فهو دون الحبائب
